THE LINDER LETTER

THIS ELECTION IS DIFFERENT

This election is not about President Trump. This election is about you.

The night President Trump was elected to serve his second term as president was 50 years to the day after I won my first race for the Georgia House of Representatives. Since that time, I’ve served 14 years in the Georgia House,18 years in Congress and have written and spoke on politics for another 20 or so years. I’m old.

There were times during those years when I thought I was pretty important, but then my wife would always remind me of Bill Hudnut. Bill was elected to Congress from Indiana in 1972. He said the first call he received after being elected to Congress was from a lady complaining about her garbage collection. He said, Ma’am, I’ve just been elected to serve you in the Congress of the United States of America. Don’t you think you should call the sanitation department? She said, I really didn’t want to go that high.

Since that night 50 years ago there have been 13 presidential elections and 12 off-year elections. And, as I recall, every one of them was the most important election of our lifetimes.

This election is different.

Let me begin by saying something that may surprise you. This election isn’t about Donald Trump. This election is about you. I know a lot of you have made up your minds about President Trump and nothing I say here is going to change that. That’s fine. I’m not here to talk about him. I’m here to ask you to look past him, at what’s been happening to the party that used to compete with him. Because whatever you think of the past, the ballot in front of you this year is, more than anything, about you and the future.
Thirty years ago, we fought Bill Clinton over welfare, healthcare, crime, the environment, taxes and abortion among other things.

There were “Blue Dog Democrats” who leaned conservative and liberal Republicans who leaned to the left, and all of the debates were fierce, but healthy, and all were among people of good will.

The Democrats sincerely wanted to improve the lives of Americans and were also sincere in believing that the way to do so was through more government programs. A good example was the Clinton Crime Bill that insisted on midnight basketball leagues with mandated diversity among the players and teams. Republicans were more inclined to punish wrong doers. We believed different things. But we debated them honestly.

Republicans also want to improve the lives of Americans but we believe that the way to do that is by creating businesses and increasing the number of jobs and increasing the size of the economy. We believe, as President Kennedy believed, that a rising tide lifts all boats.

Whatever happened to the party of John Kennedy? The party of Harry Truman, Hubert Humphrey and Bill Clinton?

Truman began the containment of the Soviet Union and integrated the armed forces by executive order, and did both without batting an eye to the right or the left.

Hubert Humphrey was a Cold War liberal who never apologized for hating communism. He saw the Democrat Party of Minnesota infested with Communists and formed the Democrat Farmer Labor Party which persists today. He never once apologized for America.

And Bill Clinton — whatever I said about him thirty years ago, and I said plenty — stood in front of Congress in 1996 and told his own party, “The era of big government is over.” He signed a welfare reform bill and a balanced budget to prove he meant it.

I didn’t agree with these men on most things. But the debate was always inside a framework of a shared America. They believed in a strong military and a dangerous world. They believed work was better than a welfare check. They believed that Communism was an enemy, not a misunderstood alternative. We could fight about taxes and spending the way families fight about money, but inside the same house. And all of them – and all of us – were for secure borders.

In any one of the previous 12 off-year elections one side or the other would win and the debate would again be as to how big or how little to tax and spend. How big or little the government’s role in our lives should be. And we survived.

This election is different.

This past year, Democratic Socialists of America candidates won the New York City mayor’s race and then, months later, in primaries unseated sitting Democratic members of Congress. Adriano Espaillat, chairman of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and a long time New York City political leader, was defeated by Darializa Avila Chevalier. No one saw it coming. Chevalier had founded a group whose stated aim was “the total eradication of western civilization.” Won’t it be interesting to see her take the oath to defend the Constitution.

In Colorado, 29-year-old Democratic Socialist Melat Kiros defeated thirty-year incumbent Diana DeGette. The Mayor of Seattle is a Democratic Socialist as well as the likely winners in November in Washington DC and Los Angeles. The mayor of New York City went on national television and said that a democratic socialist can win any office in America. He may be right.

We now have a radical Islamist leading in the race for the United States Senate in Michigan. His principal advisor is a man who believes that the US deserved 9-11 and that the US is worse than al Qaida in the world.

The analysts will tell you these wins so far are mostly in the bluest ground in America, and that winning a primary in Manhattan isn’t the same as winning a seat Republicans and Democrats both have to fight for. That’s a fair point. But the direction of the Democrat Party is clear. The energy, the money, the volunteers, and now the elected candidates are moving one way. That train has left the station and normal Democrats are racing to get on board.

Democrat Congressman Tom Suozzi from New York formed Promise to America to unite Democrats around four basic declarations.

We are capitalists not socialists. We want safety not lawlessness. We are mainstream not extreme. We are proud, not ashamed of America. Just 13 out of 212 members of the House signed on.

Analysts tell us that Democratic Socialists are not Communists. However, just before the Fourth of July, Ashik Siddique, co-chair of The Democratic Socialists of America appeared on The Will Cain Show. He said, “Our goal is Communism.” Over half of the Board of Directors of the Democratic Socialists of America self-identify as Communists. A recent poll concluded that 67% of Democrats prefer Socialism over Capitalism.

I live by a simple rule – when someone tells you who they are – believe them.

Just eight years ago Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez defeated the Chairman of the Democratic Caucus for a seat in the US House of Representatives. She was the first recruit of the Democrat Socialists and was dismissed as a lightweight. Today she is in the top rank of Democrats for the presidential nomination in 2028. Other than bartending, this is her first job. She is 36 years old.

Before her ascension, Chuck Schumer was one of the adults in the room. He was for secure borders and a secure Israel. He now shrinks in her presence and she will take his senate seat if she doesn’t run for president. He is fully on board the train. Quaking at every stop, but on board.

Ten years ago, abortion remained the central organizing principle of the Democrat Party. Today it has to get in line behind support for Gaza, hate against Jews, mutilating children, boys in girls’ bathrooms, men having babies and punishment of success – and, of course, Communism. Everyone in the Party must get on board or get left behind.

This election is different.

And this election will have a direct impact on your life. When Joe Biden was elected, his first actions were to stop the building of the Keystone Pipeline and end the sale of oil leases. Oil, being a futures market, quickly spiked because the future did not look good. Everything you buy is brought to you by oil and the cost of living spiked.

The trillion-dollar infrastructure bill that passed in 2021 was largely a bill to fund green energy projects. Increasing regulations to deal with the climate change myth increased the cost of everything you buy also, including the cost of housing.

The border was opened up completely, the UN and other NGOs situated themselves in Panama organizing foreigners to come to the US. We gave hundreds of millions of dollars to them to help usher 15 to 20 million new people into our country costing local and state governments billions of dollars and increasing the crimes against American citizens. A working paper from the Fed concluded that 30% of the increase in the cost of new housing was caused by those immigrants.

Our Department of Justice not only spent three years and tens of millions of dollars trying to put Donald Trump in jail, they also indicted 72 others who either worked for him or aided his election. They also spied on Catholic churches, prosecuted pro-lifers, deployed the FBI against parents at school board meetings - and tapped the phones of their political enemies.

And when Donald Trump was elected, the Biden Administration spent the next 76 days before Trump’s inauguration shoveling money out the door to get it out of his reach.

$93 billion was given away by the energy department. According to Secretary of Energy, Chris Wright, many of these late-stage loans were being directed toward companies that “had no clear business plan or path to financial viability.”

Not to be outdone, the EPA shoveled $20 billion out to a Citibank custodial account to be drawn down by 8 NGOs for green energy projects. One of the recipient NGOs, Power Forward Communities, was organized by Stacy Abrams just prior to the grant. She had $100 in its account.

The EPA modified the grant agreements right before the transition to legally strip the agency of its own oversight powers. The unique structure allowed the eight NGOs to withdraw the money out of the Citibank accounts without requiring any EPA approval or even having a serious plan.

Fortunately, Lee Zeldin caught the fraud, froze the money and is in the process of trying to recover it. They are, of course, suing him.

The world we are looking at today is radically different than the world we lived in just two years ago. Our borders are no longer even a point of discussion. Contact with illegals at our borders is down about 97% and over 3 million have been removed.

Our tax bill is permanent and relief for middle class Americans regarding tips, overtime and Social Security is secure.

The EPA rollback of the 2009 endangerment finding on global warming will save American taxpayers and manufacturers over $1.3 trillion in compliance costs, and lower the average cost of a new vehicle roughly $2,400. In addition, there are new lifelines for the oil, gas and coal industries and finally – that mud puddle that forms by the barn after every rain will no longer be considered a wetland that must be protected by the EPA.

Iran, for all the debate over the war, is no longer the imminent threat it has been for 47 years. Their nuclear capability has been neutralized. Their offensive capabilities no longer exist and Hamas, Hezbollah and the Houthis are on their own. Seven presidents have watched while tens of thousands have been killed across the globe. That is over. They still, however, chant Death to America.

When someone tells you who they are – believe them.

And, of course, corruption: Hospice care, child care, adult care, unemployment compensation, organ and tissue transplants, autism care, Covid loans and student loans have all been found to be riddled with fraud. American taxpayers have even been funding a civil war in Somalia. Pure fraud has been estimated to be in the hundreds of billions of dollars a year. Not a single Democrat has even spoken out about it. That is all coming to an end under the task force let by Vice President Vance.

And, most importantly, a world that has been moving inexorably toward a new world order for 70 years no longer is. The WTO is weak the WHO is neutered, the WEF is laughable, the UN is broke and the International Court has been told by Secretary Rubio that we just aren’t interested in playing, thank you very much. Nationhood is back.

Just as in the security of the border, all of this didn’t take another Congressional law, it just took another president. We are once again respected – and a little bit feared – in the world.

This election is different.

If the Democrats win this election and re-take the Congress, expect every issue we have corrected – the world, the border, the economy, regulations, taxes, green energy scams as well as child mutilation, boys in girls’ sports and punishment of success and, who knows, perhaps even rampant corruption, to return – with a vengeance.

Expect to see congressional investigations into conservatives and every conservative idea. And, of course, another impeachment or two.

Expect their most desired change in 2021, HR1, to return. It is a total re-write of election laws across the country.

We have been engaged in a knock-down drag-out battle over whether one has to be a citizen to vote in our elections and to have a photo ID to prove you are who you claim to be.

We are told by the Democrats and their propaganda arm, the Legacy Media, that election law is a matter for state legislatures. However, their HR1 totally subsumes the states’ role and eliminates voter ID, even in states that have passed it. It expands mail-in voting and ballot harvesting. It also provides for federal funding of campaigns. Every dollar raised by a candidate in amounts below $200 will receive a 6 to 1 match by the taxpayer. Food stamps for politicians!

In the 2024 election AOC would have qualified for a gift from you of more than 120 million dollars. You can do a lot of damage with 120 million dollars. In 2016 Bernie Sanders would have qualified for just under an additional billion dollars.

That did not pass in 2021 because 2 Democrat Senators refused to vote to eliminate the filibuster. Those two Senators are no longer there. Today, if they win, the filibuster will be gone on opening day and HR 1 will pass. We will also have statehood for Washington DC, Puerto Rico and Guam giving the Democrats six more senators.

The Supreme Court will be expanded to at least 13 members giving the Left a 7 to 6 majority immediately. Let us welcome 4 more Ketanji Brown Jacksons to the Court.

The media tell us, of course, that this is all speculation.

I repeat: When someone tells you who they are and what they intend to do – believe them.

Which brings me back to why I didn’t want to make this about one man. Presidents come and go. Policies last forever.

EVERYONE is angry today about our healthcare system. It is too costly, too distant and too out of control. It is the direct result of a policy decision taken by the Democrat Party when they had a huge majority in the House and a filibuster-proof Senate. The government decides what you must insure and who will provide it. The government will decide. Not you.

If you are a 59-year-old single woman seeking health insurance today you must pay to insure for hair transplants, HIV/Aids treatment, obstetrics and pediatric dentistry. Would you rather not insure for matters that don’t affect you? Your government knows best.

And more is coming. For many years what starts in California ultimately finds its way to Washington DC. Fifty years ago, it was the tax revolt and proposition 13. Today it is a series of proposals that are just revolting.

California has given us five examples just this year.

A young independent journalist named Nick Shirley went to California and filmed taxpayer-funded hospice and daycare corruption — the same kind of corruption he found in Minnesota and New York. The response from Sacramento wasn’t to investigate the fraud. It was to shut down investigations. The state will decide what is and is not corruption. Not you.

California now bars schools from requiring staff to tell a parent if their child asks to be treated as a different gender at school. Supporters say it protects kids in unsafe homes. The state will decide about your child’s needs. Not you.

California recently created the first state agency in America built to verify whether you descended from an enslaved person, as a qualifying test for state benefits in housing, education, and economic opportunity. The state will decide who was enslaved and who will benefit. Not you.

A new state law this year lets the state override local zoning and allow multi-story apartment buildings in neighborhoods zoned for single families. You may think that’s good housing policy. You may not. But the state will decide on your zoning. Not you.

California voters will decide this November on a one-time 5% tax on the assets of any resident worth over a billion dollars. You may think – a billionaire can afford it. But it will be coming to you soon.

The plan doesn’t just tax what you own — it presumes you own whatever you control. Google’s Sergey Brin owns about 5% of Alphabet stock, but his special shares give him voting control over a quarter of the company. Under the plan’s own language, that voting control — not his actual ownership — is what gets taxed. A quarter of a $4.2 trillion company, taxed at 5%, comes to $52.5 billion. To raise that in cash he’d have to sell over $80 billion in stock, about 60% of his holdings, pay tens of billions in federal and state capital gains tax on the sale itself, and crater the share price on the way out the door. Brin and his co-founder didn’t wait around to find out what might happen in the future. They left the state.

Today that line is drawn at a billion dollars. Nobody who has ever watched a tax threshold in this country believes it will stay there. And it’s coming. To a city near you.

Five examples. Five different subjects — journalism, your child, your history, your city, your money. One answer to all of them. They decide. Not you.

So let me tell you why “who decides” is not an abstraction to me. It is the story of my own life. I grew up in a small town in northern Minnesota near two Chippewa Indian reservations. The Indian children went to school with us. Every fifth-grade class I can recall had an Indian child at the top of the class. They were smart. They were artistic. They didn’t graduate. Teen age pregnancies, crime, alcohol, violence. There were no fathers in those homes.

For over a hundred years America gathered the Indians up onto reservations and bureaucrats told them where to go to school, which dentist and doctor to see, where to buy school clothes, and we paid the bill. Soon, the influence of the breadwinner was replaced by a bureaucrat with a government check and the breadwinner left.

I’m the only white man who ever played baseball with the Inger Indians. I was the catcher on that team and we had a pitcher named Richie Robinson. Richie had a curve ball that looked like it was coming at you from third base. He was offered a minor league contract that summer. He didn’t know if he should take it. I said, “Richie, you’re 26 years old and you’ve never had a job. They want to pay you to play baseball. Take the contract.”

Six weeks later he was back home. I asked him what happened. He said, “I just couldn’t make it. I didn’t know how to get an apartment so the owner had to help me. I kept getting confused about changing buses. I didn’t know if I should get a black and white or color T.V. I just couldn’t make all those decisions.”

At age 17 I realized that government decisions had stolen from them the ability to make decisions about their own lives.

Richie Robinson, Esica Ogema, David Cloud, Johnny Wakanabo, Tom Bowstring. They all died young. Not because government did too little. Because government did too much.

Having done so well with the American Indian we replicated the reservation in every major city in America with the very same results. Teen age pregnancies, crime, violence, drugs. No fathers in those homes. Not because government did too little. Because government did too much.

In spite of the total collapse of communism and socialism around the world, the Democratic Socialists of America honestly believe that more government will fix the problems that government has created. They don’t trust your decisions. They trust theirs.

They do not know – as we know – that the human being dreams – not for one more government program – but for freedom. The Soviet Union learned that in just 69 years.

I refuse to say that this election is the most important election of our lifetimes. But this election is different.

If they win, the world will never be the same. And it won’t be just how or when you can get healthcare. This will be a new debate, not over how much or how little. This will be a debate over what. And they will decide what.

Bill Buckley founded the National Review in 1955. For the next 35 years, Buckley and his team, including for a time former Soviet spy and National Review senior editor Whittaker Chambers, were in fierce resistance against the threat of communism to the United States.

In 1954 Chambers had written a letter to Buckley laying out his view that the threat of communism was not from without, but from within. Chambers wrote, “It is idle to speak of saving Western Civilization because Western Civilization is already a wreck from within. That is why we can hope to do little more than snatch a fingernail off a saint on the rack, or a handful of ashes from the faggots and bury them secretly, in a flowerpot, against that day ages hence, when a few men begin again to dare to believe that there once was something else. That something else is thinkable and need some evidence of what it was and the fortifying knowledge that there were those who, at the great nightfall, took loving thought to preserve the tokens of hope and truth.”

I began this by saying that this is not about Donald Trump. This is about you. The future will come down to you and your neighbors and your friends. Are you the little platoons in the cities, in the towns, in the neighborhoods, who dare to believe that the tokens of hope and truth are worth saving? I think that you are. I think you will look at the choices beyond the personalities. I think you will conclude that this election is different and rally to turn out the communists among us and choose instead freedom. And my grandchildren and great-grandchildren will say thank you. As will I. Thank you.

< Be John Marshall
< Born 1755, log cabin, Virginia frontier
< Fourth of fifteen children
< Your father surveys land alongside George Washington
< Formal schooling: fourteen months total
< The Revolution starts. You enlist at nineteen.
< Valley Forge. You survive the winter that kills 2,500 men.
< War ends. You teach yourself law in six weeks of lectures.
< Virginia bar, 1780. You build a practice from nothing.
< Elected to the state legislature four times
< Washington offers you Attorney General. You decline.
< Adams offers you Supreme Court. You accept.
< Chief Justice, 1801. You will hold the seat for 34 years.
< Marbury v. Madison, 1803. You invent judicial review out of thin air.
< The Constitution does not give courts the power to strike down laws
< You give it to them anyway
< 1,100 opinions written. You author over half personally.
< You outlast four presidents, three wars, one attempted impeachment
< Die in office, 1835. The Liberty Bell cracks ringing at your funeral.

The man with fourteen months of schooling became the most powerful judge in American history.

He created a power the Founders never wrote down, then made it seem inevitable.

Every court that has ever struck down a law is living in the world John Marshall built.

text:
Contrary to a popular myth, Nevada never had ten-foot red-haired cannibals. That tale is modern. The Paiute story under it is older, and stranger, and it never mentions giants.

The Northern Paiute lived on the Humboldt Sink, where the river dies in the western Nevada desert. They fished the lakes, hunted waterfowl, and gathered seeds and roots. They had no horses until the 1800s. In 1883 Sarah Winnemucca Hopkins, daughter of Chief Winnemucca, published Life Among the Piutes, one of the first books by a Native American author, and put her father’s story in it.

He called the enemy people-eaters. They made war on the Paiute, and in a fight they caught arrows overhead and shot the same arrows back. Some were taken into Paiute families. They would not live as Paiute. The war ran about three years. She puts their number at about 2,600. The survivors fled into brush above Humboldt Lake. The Paiute fired the brush. The people-eaters built tule boats, took to the lake, and nearly starved for want of fire. One night they landed on the east shore and entered a cave the Paiute had not known was there. 

They spoke the same language. Asked to stop eating people like coyotes or beasts, they refused. The Paiute filled the mouth with wood, set it alight, and offered to put the fire out if they gave up. No answer came. Ten days later the smell told her third or fifth great-grandfather that the people inside were dead. Neighbors then called her people Say-do-carah (say-doh-KAH-rah), conqueror or enemy. She said the dead had reddish hair, and that a mourning dress trimmed with it had stayed in her family. No height. No island. No giants.

Later tellings named them Si-Te-Cah (see-teh-KAH), tule-eaters, and grew them into giants on rafts. The growth came from a miner’s memory of one red-haired mummy about 6 feet 6 inches tall, from 1930s Nevada newspaper claims of 8-foot and 10-foot skeletons, and from tourist displays around Lovelock.

The cave is real. Guano miners stripped the floor in 1911. Llewellyn Loud excavated in 1912, and again with Mark Harrington in 1924. About 10,000 objects came out: tule duck decoys about 2,000 years old, nets, baskets, ordinary sandals, and human remains of normal size. Archaeologists call that occupation the Lovelock culture, ancient Great Basin hunter-gatherers, not another race. Dry caves turn dark hair red. A few split bones have been read as rare marrow processing, not a cannibal people. The newspaper skeletons were never kept.

The Paiute remembered a red-haired enemy. The cave held ordinary people. The giants came later.

text:
The Scriptures from the OT to the NT very clearly show that Jesus the Christ is YHWH, just as the Father is YHWH, and that the Spirit is YHWH, and that there is no God but YHWH.

Show me how and where the Nicene Creed is incompatible with any of this.

I. The Father is YHWH
1. Deut 32:6 — YHWH "your Father" who "created you,"
2. Isa 63:16 — "You, O YHWH, are our Father, our Redeemer from of old is your name," 
3. Isa 64:8 — "But now, O YHWH, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter,"
4. Jer 3:19 — YHWH says Israel would call him "My Father" 
5. Mal 2:10 — "Have we not all one Father? Has not one God created us?" 
6. Ps 89:26 — "my Father, my God, and the Rock of my salvation."
7. 1 Cor 8:6 — Paul splits the Shema ("one God... one Lord") and assigns "one God" to the Father, so whatever "one God" meant in Deut 6:4, it is predicated of the Father.
8. Eph 4:6 — "one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all,"
9. John 17:3 — Jesus calls the Father "the only true God," and in John's own idiom "the true God" is YHWH (cf. 1 John 5:20).
10. Matt 11:25 — the Father as "Lord of heaven and earth," a title belonging to YHWH alone (Gen 14:22).
11. Rev 4:8, 11 — the one on the throne, distinguished from the Lamb in ch. 5, is hailed with Isaiah's trisagion and Exodus's covenant name formula.
12. Rom 15:6 — "the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ"
13. Heb 1:1–2 — the God who "spoke to our fathers by the prophets" (i.e., YHWH throughout the OT) is the Father who now speaks by the Son.
14. James 3:9 — men are made "in the likeness of God," and the one praised as such is "the Lord and Father."
15. ... 

II. The Son is YHWH
A. Direct predication of θεός / divine titles
1. John 1:1 — "the Word was God," where the anarthrous predicate theos is qualitative, ascribing the full divine nature to the Word while distinguishing him from the Father he is "with."
2. John 1:18 — the best-attested reading is monogenēs theos, "the unique one, himself God," making the Son as truly theos as the Father whom no one has seen.
3. John 20:28 — "my Lord and my God" 
4. Rom 9:5 — "the Christ, who is God over all, blessed forever"
5. Titus 2:13 — "our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ"
6. 2 Pet 1:1 — "our God and Savior Jesus Christ"
7. Heb 1:8 — the Father himself addresses the Son with Ps 45:6, "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever."
8. Isa 9:6 — the child born is titled El Gibbor, "Mighty God," the very title Isaiah applies to YHWH one chapter later (10:21).
9. Matt 1:23 — Jesus is named Immanuel, "God with us," in fulfillment of Isaiah's sign.
10. Col 2:9 — "in him the whole fullness of deity (theotēs) dwells bodily," asserting not delegated divinity but the divine essence itself.
11. Jude 4 — "our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ," where despotēs plus "only" is exclusivist language elsewhere reserved for God.

B. OT YHWH texts applied to Jesus 
12. Isa 40:3 → Mark 1:3 — "Prepare the way of YHWH" 
13. Mal 3:1 → Mark 1:2 — YHWH says "the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple,"
14. Joel 2:32 → Rom 10:13 — "everyone who calls on the name of YHWH shall be saved," which Paul applies to confessing Jesus as Lord in vv. 9–13 without adjustment.
15. Isa 45:23 → Phil 2:10–11 — the oath that every knee shall bow to YHWH is fulfilled in every knee bowing to Jesus.
16. Isa 8:13–14 → 1 Pet 2:8; Rom 9:33 — YHWH of hosts is the sanctuary and the stone of stumbling, and both apostles identify that stone as Jesus Christ.
17. Isa 6:1–10 → John 12:41 — John says Isaiah "saw his glory and spoke of him," referring to Jesus, so the enthroned YHWH of Isa 6 is the pre-incarnate Son.
18. Zech 12:10 → John 19:37; Rev 1:7 — YHWH says "they will look on me whom they have pierced," fulfilled at the cross of Jesus.
19. Ps 102:25–27 → Heb 1:10–12 — a psalm addressed explicitly to YHWH the unchanging Creator is quoted by the Father as spoken to the Son.
20. Isa 44:6; 48:12 → Rev 1:17; 2:8; 22:13 — YHWH's self-designation "the first and the last, besides me there is no god" is taken by Jesus as his own title.
21. Ps 110:1 → Matt 22:44 — David calls his own descendant "my Lord," a superiority Jesus presses as unanswerable on merely human messianic assumptions.
22. Deut 10:17 / Ps 136:3 → Rev 17:14; 19:16 — "Lord of lords and King of kings," a divine superlative title, is worn by the Lamb.
23. Isa 43:11; Hos 13:4 → Titus 2:13; 2 Pet 1:11 — YHWH says "besides me there is no savior," yet Jesus is repeatedly and unqualifiedly called Savior.
24. Exod 3:14 / Isa 41:4; 43:10 → John 8:24, 58; 13:19 — Jesus' absolute egō eimi matches the LXX of Isaiah's divine self-identification, and his hearers' attempt to stone him shows they heard it that way.
25. Isa 42:8 → John 17:5 — YHWH refuses to give his glory to another, yet the Son asks for the glory he shared with the Father before the world existed.
26. Jer 17:10 → Rev 2:23 — "I, YHWH, search the heart and test the mind" is claimed verbatim by the risen Christ.
27. Num 21:5–6 → 1 Cor 10:9 — Paul says Israel in the wilderness tested Christ, identifying him with the YHWH they provoked.

C. Divine prerogatives and attributes
28. Mark 2:5–7 — Jesus forgives sins not committed against him, and the scribes correctly reason that only God can do this.
29. John 5:18 — his hearers understood "my Father" plus Sabbath authority as "making himself equal with God," and John reports the inference without disowning it.
30. John 5:23 — the Son is to be honored "just as" the Father is honored, an equality of worship no creature may receive.
31. Col 1:16–17 — all things in heaven and earth were created by him and for him, and in him all things hold together, which is creatorship, not organization of preexisting matter.
32. John 1:3 — "without him was not any thing made that was made," a universal negative excluding the Son from the class of made things.
33. Heb 1:3 — he is the radiance of God's glory and the exact imprint (charaktēr) of his hypostasis, and he upholds the universe by his word.
34. Heb 13:8 — "the same yesterday and today and forever," ascribing divine immutability, which YHWH claims as his distinctive in Mal 3:6.
35. Matt 18:20; 28:20 — he promises personal presence wherever two or three gather and to the end of the age, which requires omnipresence.
36. Matt 25:31–46 — he sits as eschatological judge of all nations, an office the OT reserves to YHWH.
37. Rev 5:13–14 — the Lamb receives the identical worship as the one on the throne from every creature, and the elders fall down in worship.
38. Matt 12:8 — "the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath," and the Sabbath belongs to YHWH who instituted it.
39. Acts 7:59–60 — Stephen prays to Jesus to receive his spirit, echoing Ps 31:5 addressed to YHWH.
40. 1 Cor 8:6 — "one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things," placing Jesus inside the Shema under the title kyrios, the LXX rendering of YHWH.
41. Micah 5:2 — the ruler from Bethlehem has "goings forth from of old, from the days of eternity."
42. ... 

III. The Spirit is YHWH
A. Identified with God directly
1. Acts 5:3–4 — Peter's parallel ("lied to the Holy Spirit" / "not lied to men but to God") equates the two without any softening particle
2. 1 Cor 3:16 — "you are God's temple and God's Spirit dwells in you," where the indwelling Spirit is what makes the building God's temple.
3. 1 Cor 6:19–20 — the body is "a temple of the Holy Spirit," and a temple is defined by the deity who inhabits it.
4. 2 Cor 3:17 — "now the Lord is the Spirit," written in an exposition of Exod 34 where "the Lord" is YHWH.
5. 2 Sam 23:2–3 — "The Spirit of YHWH spoke by me... the God of Israel said," setting Spirit-speech and God-speech in synonymous parallelism.

B. The Spirit speaks OT words attributed to YHWH
6. Ps 95:7–11 → Heb 3:7–11 — words spoken by YHWH in the first person ("as I swore in my wrath") are introduced with "as the Holy Spirit says."
7. Jer 31:33–34 → Heb 10:15–17 — a covenant oracle marked "declares YHWH" is credited to the Holy Spirit's testimony.
8. Isa 6:8–10 → Acts 28:25–27 — the commission Isaiah received from Adonai enthroned is said to have been spoken "by the Holy Spirit."
9. Exod 17:2, 7 → Acts 5:9 — testing YHWH at Massah becomes, in Peter's mouth, "testing the Spirit of the Lord."
10. Isa 63:10–14 — Israel "grieved his Holy Spirit," and the Spirit who led them is interchangeably called YHWH's presence and arm.

C. Divine attributes and works
11. Ps 139:7–10 — there is nowhere to flee from the Spirit, which is omnipresence, an incommunicable divine attribute.
12. 1 Cor 2:10–11 — the Spirit "searches the depths of God" and knows God's thoughts as a man's own spirit knows his, implying omniscience of the divine essence.
13. Heb 9:14 — Christ offered himself "through the eternal Spirit," ascribing eternality.
14. Gen 1:2; Job 33:4; Ps 104:30 — the Spirit hovers over creation, makes man, and renews the face of the ground.
15. Luke 1:35 — the Holy Spirit and "the power of the Most High" stand in parallel as the agent of the incarnation.
16. Rom 8:11 — the Spirit raises the dead, a work Scripture reserves to God.
17. Matt 12:31–32 — blasphemy against the Spirit is uniquely unforgivable, which presupposes he is a divine person and not a force or influence.
18. ...

IV. YHWH alone is God
1. Deut 4:35 — "YHWH is God; there is no other besides him"
2. Deut 4:39 — "YHWH is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath; there is no other," a cosmic, not merely local, exclusivity.
3. Deut 6:4 — the Shema, "YHWH our God, YHWH is one," the confessional heart of biblical monotheism.
4. Deut 32:39 — "See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god beside me," in a song God commanded Israel to memorize.
5. Isa 43:10 — "Before me no god was formed, nor shall there be any after me," which excludes both a God who preceded the Father and any who might later attain that status.
6. Isa 44:6 — "I am the first and I am the last; besides me there is no god," spoken by Israel's King and Redeemer.
7. Isa 44:8 — "Is there a God besides me? There is no Rock; I know not any," where God pleads ignorance of any other deity.
8. Isa 44:24 — "I am YHWH... who stretched out the heavens alone, who spread out the earth by myself," excluding a council of gods from the work of creation.
9. Isa 45:5 — "I am YHWH, and there is no other, besides me there is no God," addressed to Cyrus who did not know him.
10. Isa 45:14, 18, 21, 22 — a fourfold drumbeat of "there is no other" across a single chapter, culminating in a universal call to be saved by him.
11. Isa 46:9 — "I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like me," grounding the claim in his unique power to declare the end from the beginning.
12. Isa 37:16, 20 — Hezekiah prays "you alone are God of all the kingdoms," precisely because Assyria's gods were no gods at all.
13. Isa 42:8 — "I am YHWH; that is my name; my glory I give to no other," ruling out shared divine glory with any second deity.
14. 1 Kgs 8:60 — Solomon's temple prayer aims at all peoples knowing "that YHWH is God; there is no other."
15. 2 Sam 7:22 — "there is none like you, and there is no God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears."
16. 2 Kgs 19:15 — "You are the God, you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made heaven and earth."
17. Neh 9:6 — "You are YHWH, you alone. You have made heaven... and you preserve all of them."
18. Ps 86:10 — "you are great and do wondrous things; you alone are God."
19. Jer 10:10–11 — YHWH is "the true God... the everlasting King," and any gods who did not make the heavens will perish from under them.
20. Hos 13:4 — "you know no God but me, and besides me there is no savior."
21. Mark 12:29–32 — Jesus affirms the Shema as the first commandment, and the scribe's gloss ("he is one, and there is no other besides him") draws Jesus' approval.
22. John 17:3 — eternal life is knowing "the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent."
23. 1 Cor 8:4–6 — "there is no God but one," stated in full awareness that pagans acknowledge many so-called gods.
24. Gal 3:20 — "God is one," used as a settled premise in an argument about the law's mediation.
25. Rom 3:30 — "God is one," grounding the justification of both Jew and Gentile by faith.
26. 1 Tim 2:5 — "there is one God, and one mediator between God and men."
27. 1 Tim 1:17; 6:15–16 — "the only God," "the blessed and only Sovereign," "who alone has immortality."
28. James 2:19 — "you believe that God is one; you do well," conceding monotheism as the baseline even demons hold.
29. Jude 25 — "to the only God, our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord."
30. ...

text:
Yes. There are documented criminal cases in which people paid homeless individuals small amounts of cash or goods tied to voter registration and ballot-petition signatures, mainly on Los Angeles’ Skid Row. Direct, proven cases of a political party systematically paying homeless people to cast ballots for a specific candidate are thinner and often rest on allegations rather than convictions.

The clearest court records involve paid petition circulators, not party payrolls. Circulators are typically independent contractors paid by “coordinators” or signature-management firms for each valid signature from a registered voter on initiatives, referendums, or recalls. Because payment depended on the signer being registered, some circulators paid unregistered homeless people to register first.

•In 2026, Brenda Lee Brown Armstrong, a longtime petition circulator, agreed to plead guilty to a federal felony of paying another person to register to vote. Prosecutors said she regularly offered Skid Row homeless people $2–$3, cigarettes, or phone cords to sign petitions, and beginning in 2025 also paid them to complete registration forms—sometimes listing her own former address. She was later sentenced to probation and community service. The investigation followed undercover video; the coordinators who paid her per signature were not named in the public charging documents.

•In a separate 2026 federal indictment, James Brass and two others were charged with paying Skid Row homeless people to forge signatures on ballot petitions using identities taken from voter rolls. Prosecutors said Brass received about $41,600 from a petition-management company.

•In 2018–2020, Los Angeles County prosecutors charged nine people with offering Skid Row homeless residents about $1 and cigarettes for false or forged signatures on ballot petitions and voter-registration forms during the 2016 and 2018 cycles. Several pleaded guilty or no contest (including Norman Hall, who received a year in jail). Officials described the apparent motive as financial rather than partisan; the petitions covered initiatives linked to various interests.

Paying or offering something of value to induce someone to vote, or to register in certain circumstances, is illegal under federal law (including 18 U.S.C. § 597) and California election law. Homeless people who meet citizenship, age, and residency rules can register and vote; the offense is the payment or the use of false information.

Separate from these convictions, videos circulated in June 2026 of Skid Row residents claiming they were paid a few dollars and told to vote for Mayor Karen Bass or Councilmember Nithya Raman. Los Angeles County election officials publicly disputed at least some of the claims (one interviewee was registered in Inglewood, not Los Angeles), and the Los Angeles Times described related broader fraud assertions as unsupported. Those claims have not produced the same guilty pleas as the petition cases.
Older anecdotes exist—machine-politics stories about flophouse or mission residents being given cigarettes or alcohol around elections (for example, a 2000 Milwaukee incident involving a Democratic donor that investigators did not establish as a proven quid pro quo)—but they are less formalized than the Skid Row prosecutions. In short, paying vulnerable people for election-related signatures and registrations has been repeatedly charged and admitted; evidence that parties themselves bought candidate votes from the homeless is mostly allegation rather than adjudicated fact.

text:
OttoGeoGraphica
August, 1998
Old Arbat Street
Moscow, Russia
(film camera photo)

Old Arbat Street offers a variety of French, Italian, and local cuisine. I spend three weeks in Moscow, and every afternoon, a gathering of expats are ordering nachos and margaritas at Jose Cuevo’s Cantina. Living thirteen years in Southern California where mom-and-pop Baja California cuisine is priced competitively at almost every street corner restaurant, or every remodeled old Denny’s, I soon grew tired of the thought of eating Mexican food every afternoon in, of all places, Moscow, Russia, so after three days of this, I begin to excuse myself and venture toward the metro.

As I stroll, a pink poodle has staked a claim to one side of the street, dancing for kopecks, while a genteel, middle-aged clown is doing a somewhat desperate interpretative dance on the other side. In the background artisans are bartering their masterpieces—all prices negotiable—to the passing international clientele.

Crossing over a major thoroughfare, I’m accosted by a tattered, aged Muscovite. He has a plastic shopping bag in one hand and a tin cup in another. He offers me a drink from the cup, a toast. For within the bag is a half-full bottle of vodka, along with some remnants of a broken bottle. Staggering, he recovers the base of the broken bottle much larger than a rocks glass. The sharp, jagged edges would challenge the will of any true alcoholic, but he pours a fresh shot into it in stride and pours another shot for me into the tin. I refuse. Not because I have an aversion to vodka, and not because I’m already slightly buzzed from the agave nectar of Mexico, but rather because Western culture, or more honestly, personal social mores, would not permit such a pure and kind exchange with a total stranger. He asked, in broken English, my nationality, and when I stated it from a position of prestige rather than arrogance, he replied: “bah”. This “bah”, guttural and almost inaudible, seemed to come not from a realization of any social disparities between our persons or our cultures, but rather dismissive, as if a simple shot of vodka could solve any personal, social, or political issues we may have had. I have long since regretted accepting that cordial.

A motion picture theatre advertisement is at the entrance of the station. Adam Sandler is holding a microphone, while Drew Barrymore is admirably watching him sing. The title and names are written in bold Cyrillic. An extensive escalator descends into an architectural masterpiece: a Moscow Metro Station. To view such mosaics and sculptures housed under such elaborate arches and columns should seemingly cost a thousand times the price of a mere token. The metro cars arrive every ninety seconds.

The ride to Kropotkinskaya station is brief. More mosaics and sculptures highlight the corridor toward the ascending escalator. Upon surfacing, cathedrals define the skyline of this “godless” country, and near the steps of one, a woman sits. She is wrapped in layers of clothing, unnecessary on this comfortable August afternoon. The flesh of her hands and face are the only evidence that the mass is human. A polished, crooked cane the length of a yardstick lies nearby. One hand props her body, keeping her from a total collapse on the sidewalk. Pedestrians have to negotiate around her. A small, greasy, well-used paper sack has had its top edges rolled down to about three inches from its base. It sits just beyond the woman’s left knee. Displayed within the sack is a postcard sized, metal portrait of Mother Mary highlighted in gold. Around the picture, and suggesting a fountain without water, are assorted denominations of rubles and kopecks, also tokens and gum wrappers. She acknowledges no donation. I was sure she wouldn’t survive the winter, yet she probably did.

Making a right onto a narrow, tree-lined street, I follow the map about four blocks before arriving at a rather large, two-story, faded brown home: the city home of Leo Tolstoy. The lot includes a detached stable/garage building of matching color, and a rather extensive garden to the south of the main house. Two cats are busy grooming themselves on a porch bench. Waxing poetically, I would like to assume these cats are the direct descendants of the original pets of Master Tolstoy, when in reality they surely are no more than a couple of strays being daily fed by the caretakers.

After Tolstoy, I opted to hail a cab. By simply raising an arm, any Muscovite who owns a car will stop, and after negotiating the cost, will drive you anywhere you want to go; “for vodka change”, as the service is called. The narrow street offered no traffic and by the time I returned to the busier avenue I was near the Metro. The old babushka woman had declined further toward the sidewalk, still unmoved, and upon my returning to Old Arbat, I noticed my tattered drinking buddy within the portal of a closed store front, standing, leaning against the window, with bag still in hand, asleep.

Bourbon and Rye Cocktails: The History of American Whiskey in 73 Recipes [A Cocktail Recipe Book]

by Robert Simonson 

Delivers by October 13 onwards

Explore the storied history of American whiskey through more than 70 bourbon- and rye-based cocktail recipes, from award-winning author and New York Times and Wall Street Journal cocktail and spirits writer Robert Simonson.

A must-have for whiskey enthusiasts and cocktail aficionados, Bourbon and Rye Cocktails chronicles the rich, centuries-long history of American whiskey and offers a curated collection of expertly crafted cocktails.

Using a timeline format with entries spanning the late eighteenth century to today, award-winning spirits writer Robert Simonson spotlights the key moments (Prohibition, the rise of modern craft distilleries), pioneering personalities (Elijah Craig, Abe Overholt), and legendary brands (Buffalo Trace, Old Forester, Maker’s Mark) in the history of American whiskey. 

Most timeline entries are accompanied by a related cocktail, for a total of 73 simple recipes contributed by some of the best bartenders in America. Recipes include riffs on classic cocktails—the Old-Fashioned, Manhattan, Mint Julep, Sazerac, Whiskey Sour—as well as new favorites such as the Barrel Hopper (refreshing and boozy with chocolate bitters and cinnamon), Autumn Leaves (a hot toddy, but cold), 

The Ninth Ward (a tropical quaff featuring fresh lime and elderflower liqueur), and Soba Sour (starring buckwheat tea, sherry, and honey).

text:
rigor heavily depends on what you study and what courses you take. for example, there are several courses at schools like Stanford, MIT, Harvard, etc. that are easier than a some courses at a school like Northeastern (which I’m not dismissing, it’s a solid school) and there are courses at Northeastern that would be harder than some classes at the aforementioned schools (and vice versa). I say this as someone who attended a top 5 school. 

At the end of the day, especially for degrees like STEM, there’s probably 50+ schools in the US (mostly well funded research universities) out there that roughly give you the same education on average, with some variance for courses the student takes and who the professors are. Besides, with the wealth of information on the Internet and AI, there isn’t necessarily hidden education that you’re getting academically from these schools. Any person can go find UChicago lectures or Brown lectures or MIT lectures for free these days.

What the top schools offer are a massive network of students and alumni, research opportunities with well-known professors, and brand value to your resume. The other top factor I would consider in a school is location (being near a top metropolitan city like Boston, SF, NYC).

text:
Quiz Show #24

Where are we going? Where can we go?

Tonight Live and interactive 
8pm AEDT

Play Dan Andrews’ video.

Ex Victorian Premier Dan Andrews said that ‘soon you will not be able to buy or trade in the economy unless you get the vaccine’. He then talks about unvaccinated people as if they are monsters who spread viruses 24/7. This is not about the vaccine. It is about freedom and control.

QU 01
Questionably, this is one of the speeches that divided Australia. Which political leader recorded the speech that said, “We’re sorry. Dan Andrews was wrong, and all of you who were kicked out of society are now warmly welcomed back, because this is Australia, and we are meant to be, and we are, One People”?

QU 02
Play Kochie video

Since then, when did the Sunrise crew/channel 7 acknowledge that they could have been wrong, and that, despite all the troubles and threats we perpetually face, Christmas in Australia has traditionally always been about, and always should be about, coming together as families?

QU 03
In a jury trial, the duty of the defence lawyer is to establish reasonable doubt.

In the last six years, many of us have been researching and/or sharing the information that has been uncovered about:

the origin of the virus
the dodgy creation of the vaccine
the lies about the vaccine’s safety and effectiveness
the excess deaths that have occurred after the rollout among the vaccinated
the fact that the unvaccinated population did not die of COVID
and more

QU 03, Part 1
If you were on this jury, where the case was “Is Big Pharma and all those involved guilty or not guilty of participating in a massive fraud?”, what verdict do you think you would reach?

QU 03, Part 2
What verdict do you think the jury would reach if the jury was fully vaccinated?

QU 04
List how many jobs you have heard of that still require you to be ‘fully vaccinated’.

QU 05
What events and policies happening in our society now make you feel concerned about our country’s future, both for you and for the next generation?

QU 06
Do you feel that the Labor Party or the Liberal Party has the drive and the policies in place to fix all these issues? (from previous question)

QU 07
Do you believe that Pauline Hanson and One Nation have the drive and the policies to fix all these issues?

QU 08
Many economic refugees leave the third world and the developing world looking for a better life. Australia was seen as the Lucky Country, where the great Australian dream was reachable. Now, for many, it is not. So if you had a hankering to leave, list the countries you could flee to that would not only accept you, but would also offer you a chance to reach the dreams you cannot achieve here in the ‘Lucky Country’.

QU 09
For those who do not want to leave, or who do not feel it is right to leave, have you toyed with the idea of setting up a new community of like-minded people here? If so, where in Australia would you like this community to be established, and why?

QU 10
Many of the ‘tribes’ that established themselves after COVID — Hoodie Heroes, My Place, and others — have struggled and even collapsed due to infighting. How would living together in one community fix the infighting problem?

QU 11
Many cultures are measured by their history and achievements. China, for example, has completely changed its cultural identity, from Little Red Book-carrying backwater communists to the tech leaders of the modern world. America has gone from the bastion of freedom and honour to a never-ending reality-show train wreck. Australia has also changed its identity (as quoted by Alex Antic). This change has been happening for a while, but it has really ramped up in the last few years.

What are some of the cultural norms that we have lost that you miss the most?

QU 12
The Romans changed the world, then collapsed into the Italians. The Napoleonic French changed the world; now the streets of Paris appear to always be on fire. The Commonwealth once appeared to rule the world; now the English are jailing their own citizens for Facebook posts.

Arguably, the base common denominator in the collapse of these superpowers was politics and corruption.

On the other hand, Argentina has travelled from a vicious dictatorship, to a corrupt economic basket case, to a thriving community that is doing well. El Salvador, too, went from one of the most corrupt and dangerous countries on the planet to one of the safest, and a tourist mecca.

Arguably, the base common denominator in these rebuilds was not just politics, but a desperate hunger among the majority of the people for dramatic and positive change.

In your opinion, how close are the majority of people in our country to demanding great change, or do you feel that this will never happen?

QU 13
The seed of great change is a vision for the future. The powerful have the vision of their 2030 agenda, which is not good for us. But their vision for their future keeps these people on track despite all the obstacles they face and the current chaos.

So if the seed of great change is a vision for the future, what sort of Australia would you not only like to live in, but also be proud to hand down to the next generation?

Remember, we are after seeds, not a complicated, detailed plan.

QU 14
If you do not like what is happening to our country now, and/or if you do not want to go where our government is taking us, then close your eyes and try to see some of the visions for a new Australia that were just put forward. When you can see this new possible future in your head, ask yourself this: 
When do we start heading there?

Michael Gray Griffith
Cafe Locked Out

text:
The dots were connected decades ago with the A.Q Khan incident. The A.Q. Khan network was a private black-market operation that sold uranium-enrichment technology and, in at least one case, a weapon design. It is the clearest documented case of a nuclear-armed state’s know-how leaking outward through commercial channels rather than through a formal government-to-government deal.

Abdul Qadeer Khan was a Pakistani metallurgist who worked in the 1970s at the URENCO enrichment consortium in the Netherlands. He returned to Pakistan with stolen centrifuge designs and supplier lists and became central to Pakistan’s own highly enriched uranium program, which produced the material for its 1998 tests. From the mid-1980s into the early 2000s he and associates reversed that procurement network: they offered centrifuge components, designs, and manufacturing know-how to foreign customers, using front companies in Dubai, Malaysia, Turkey, and elsewhere, falsified end-user documents, and intermediaries who moved both hardware and payments. Khan later said he acted with the knowledge of some Pakistani officials; Islamabad has maintained that the transfers were unauthorized. The network was exposed in 2003–2004 after the interception of a shipment bound for Libya; Khan confessed on Pakistani television in February 2004 and was placed under house arrest.

What moved, by recipient: Iran received P-1 centrifuge designs and components beginning in 1987, with further shipments of drawings and parts into the mid-1990s. Iranian officials later told the IAEA the contacts ran through intermediaries and included an offer of a more advanced P-2 design. The hardware and blueprints gave Iran a working gas-centrifuge program years earlier than an indigenous effort would have. Iran’s enrichment plants at Natanz were built around that technology lineage. The program remained under Iranian state control; it did not produce a tested weapon, but it created the enrichment capacity that later became the core of the nuclear dispute and the 2015 JCPOA limits.

North Korea received centrifuge technology and designs in the late 1990s, reportedly in exchange for missile technology that Pakistan wanted. U.S. and IAEA assessments concluded that Khan-network assistance accelerated Pyongyang’s uranium-enrichment route alongside its existing plutonium program. North Korea conducted its first nuclear test in 2006 and has since expanded both plutonium and uranium pathways; the precise contribution of the Khan-supplied centrifuges versus later indigenous work is still estimated rather than fully itemized in public sources.

Libya received the most complete package. Between 1997 and 2003 the network supplied L-1 and L-2 centrifuge components, manufacturing equipment, uranium hexafluoride, and a document set that included a Chinese-origin implosion weapon design (the same design Pakistan had received earlier). A German-owned ship, the BBC China, was intercepted in October 2003 carrying centrifuge parts destined for Libya. After the interception and Western pressure, Libya disclosed and dismantled the program in December 2003; the design documents and equipment were turned over to the United States and the IAEA. Libya never assembled a device.

Outcomes were therefore uneven. Libya’s program ended before it produced fissile material or a weapon. Iran obtained a durable enrichment capability that it still operates, subject to later diplomatic constraints and sanctions. North Korea obtained technology that complemented its own program and went on to test nuclear devices. No complete warhead was delivered ready-to-use. The transferable items were designs, components, materials-production equipment, and, in Libya’s case, a weapon blueprint—enough to shorten timelines by years, not enough to hand over an arsenal.

The network’s exposure led to UN Security Council Resolution 1540 on non-state proliferation, tighter export controls, and prosecutions of several intermediaries (including in Malaysia, Germany, and South Africa). Khan was freed from house arrest in 2009 and died in 2021. The episode remains the standard reference for how centrifuge technology and weapon-design information left a state program through private channels and reached three countries that either pursued or, in North Korea’s case, achieved nuclear weapons. 

The bottom line is that the world is not safe as long as there are state actors that wish to annihilate their mortal enemies along with religious fanatics intent on world domination and the destruction of Israel. The Nostradamus prophecies of a Middle East centered apocalypse cause one to wonder not how it will come about, but rather when it will happen.

Many of you have come to know my mom through the education stories I’ve done, my reading initiative, or simply through the way I approach people and tell their stories. Over the years, I’ve often heard people say, “You’re so respectful and understanding,” or, “I bet your parents are so proud of you.”

I always thought about how much of that came from my mom.

Throughout my career, I’ve often been the person standing beside families during some of the hardest moments of their lives, trying to offer comfort and tell their stories with compassion. This time, I’m on the other side of that grief.

Losing my mom so suddenly has been incredibly difficult. Being a state away while chasing my dreams was never easy, but she always encouraged me to keep going and believed I could accomplish anything I set my mind to.

She taught me to help those who need it most, to keep an open mind, and to lead with compassion. So much of the person I am today is because of her.

Her loss is profound, but I know she would want me to keep chasing my dreams, keep helping people, and keep being the person she raised me to be.

Mom, I love you. I hope I continue to make you proud. ❤️

text:
This is a totally reasonable take. 

I'll offer two counters:

1. Tesla's city by city slog will never be as comprehensive as Waymo's, since they rely on high definition mapping, not just navigation mapping updates like Tesla. However unlike Tesla, Alphabet contains the world's greatest mapping field operation and nav system already, so Waymo has a huge advantage in navigation. Not insurmountable though, as we saw in the early 2010s with Apple Maps. I'm guessing Tesla will build a deeper integration between its supervising drivers and Open StreetMaps to solve this problem. We'll see.

2. My Cybertruck already drives all over rural Utah and the mountain west, without any difficulties that can't be solved by camera cleaners/design (the big one, but also steadily improving in the SW side) and some minor semantic improvements that are far easier to make than thousands of hurdles Tesla has fixed over the years. Tesla can already drive me around SLC metro area with no interventions, then a hundred miles on rural highways with me doing occasional manual speed management, then onto primitive dirt/gravel backroads with minor wash-outs and all the way down to Sand Wash Boat Launch on the Green River, and even do a decent job of parking in the unmarked gravel lot there. Waymo can't do that, but more importantly, Waymo will never be able to do that - it's not in their design brief. For this reason, I think Tesla will reach a tipping point soon where there is no city by city slog, only sudden, universal availability in the US. Meanwhile, FSD Supervised has saved me from hitting at least 4 deer over the last 2 years, including preventing a 2-fer on a pitch dark mountain drive with snow falling. Just yesterday is spotted a gray cat (in twilight though) and let it recklessly pass unharmed. It's amazing for rural safety overall.

text:
That is a good one-liner, but very poor history.

Gandhi did not simply “chase the British out” in 1947. Indian independence was the culmination of decades of nationalist pressure  in which Gandhi was enormously important combined with a long constitutional transfer of authority and a deliberately organised British withdrawal.

Britain had already transferred substantial political power under the Government of India Acts of 1919 and 1935. By 1947, Attlee could state that Indian civil administration and the Indian Armed Forces already relied “to a very large extent on Indian civilians and officers.”

The British had also been Indianising the officer corps for years. The Indian Military Academy at Dehradun opened in 1932 specifically to train Indian commissioned officers. During the Second World War the Indian Army expanded enormously, creating a large body of experienced Indian officers and men capable of serving an independent state.

In 1940 Britain formally accepted the principle that Indians should frame their own constitution. The 1942 Cripps proposals offered a post-war constitutional settlement. The 1946 Cabinet Mission then attempted to arrange the transfer of power, and an Indian Interim Government was established under Jawaharlal Nehru.

Finally, on 20 February 1947, Clement Attlee's government publicly fixed a deadline: Britain would transfer power into Indian hands no later than June 1948. Mountbatten was appointed specifically to carry out that transfer. After negotiations with Indian leaders, the timetable was accelerated to 15 August 1947.

Even the armed forces were transferred through negotiated machinery. Congress and the Muslim League agreed on arrangements for dividing the Indian Armed Forces, with a Joint Defence Council supervising the transition while British troops were withdrawn.

None of this diminishes Gandhi. His achievement was extraordinary: he transformed Indian nationalism and made non-violent mass political resistance a formidable force.

But “one half-naked Indian guy chased the British out without firing a shot” replaces history with mythology. Gandhi helped make British rule politically untenable; he did not personally evict Britain. Independence came through mass nationalism, constitutional development, wartime transformation, political negotiation and an organised British transfer of governmental and military power.

text:
Ukraine’s Operation Vivaldi offers a possible answer to the drone-created kill zone.

Instead of hunting individual FPVs, the 3rd Army Corps attacked the system behind them: logistics, command nodes, UAV crews and supporting infrastructure, while using EW, air defence and interceptor drones to suppress Russian surveillance.

The logic is simple:

Reconnaissance → communications → C2 → FPV crew → strike.

Break enough links and the battlefield becomes temporarily less transparent. This created windows for mine-clearing robots, infantry and eventually armour to move.

The important question is whether this can be repeated after Russia adapts. If it can, Vivaldi suggests that the drone battlefield has not made mechanised manoeuvre obsolete. It has made systematic suppression of the enemy’s drone network a prerequisite for manoeuvre.

text:
For 100 years, physics swore every particle picks a side. Scientists just found one that refuses both. Bosons happily pile together, like light stacking inside a laser beam. Fermions guard their space and never double up, which is why your chair holds you. Every single thing we ever measured obeyed that split. Until now.

The newcomers are called anyons. Theorists dreamed them up in the 1970s, and almost nobody expected to meet one. Then, in 2020, lab teams finally spotted them hiding inside flat, two dimensional sheets of electrons. Recently, researchers at OIST in Japan and the University of Oklahoma pushed further, finding anyons living in a single line.

Here is the simple version. In three dimensions, particles can swing around each other freely, so only two behaviors survive. In one dimension, they are trapped in a queue and cannot pass. Every meeting becomes a real collision, and fresh quantum statistics appear. Even stranger, scientists can tune these anyons, dialing them from boson-like to fermion-like at will.

No particle has ever offered a dial like that, and that flexibility is why engineers are paying close attention. Topological quantum computing rests entirely on anyons. Microsoft built its Majorana qubit program on this exact idea. Because the information is braided into the shape of their paths, small errors cannot easily destroy it, which is the biggest headache in quantum machines today.

So the thing that broke a century old rule might quietly repair the technology everyone keeps promising us. That is the part I love about science. A rule looks permanent, untouchable, carved in stone, and then nature shrugs and shows us a door we never noticed. Anyons were always there, patient, waiting for us to build better eyes. What else is sitting right beside us, unseen?

text:
1914: an epidemic was killing thousands a year across the American South, the medical establishment had ruled it an infection, and one doctor proved it was the diet. They spent the next 20 years declining to hear him.

The disease was pellagra. Skin peeling off in sheets, then the bowels, then madness, then death. Around 3 million cases and 100,000 dead by the time it was over. An official commission had just concluded it was spread by poor sanitation.

Joseph Goldberger was sent to find the germ. He walked round the orphanages and asylums where it raged and noticed the thing nobody had written down. The inmates got pellagra. The staff, in the same buildings, breathing the same air, never did. The staff ate meat, milk and eggs. The inmates got cornmeal and molasses.

So he fed two orphanages fresh meat and milk, and the pellagra went.

Then he ran it backwards. Eleven healthy prisoners in Mississippi were offered pardons to live on the corn diet. Within six months, six of them had it.

The profession still wanted its germ. So in 1916 Goldberger, his wife and his colleagues took the scabs, blood and excrement of pellagra patients, and swallowed and injected them. He called the sessions filth parties. Nobody caught anything.

Southern politicians called his work a slur on the region. Doctors went on hunting the microbe. Goldberger died in 1929, still being argued with, and the missing nutrient was finally identified in 1937. Meat is full of it.

A plague caused by taking the animal off the plate, investigated for a generation as anything else.

Medicine has never found it easy to believe a cure can sit on a plate, because nobody holds the patent on a plate.

text:
Welcoming USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72) Home: Best Viewing Locations, Beat-the-Sun Spots & Arrival Schedule

If you are heading down to the bayfront this Thursday to welcome home the sailors, aircrew, and Marines of the USS Abraham Lincoln, several key vantage points offer prime viewing.

With temperatures expected to reach the mid-80s around the bay, staying comfortable in the sun is key. The locations listed below were chosen to host our live 4K bay cameras specifically because they feature the most unobstructed, panoramic views on the water. They are also local restaurant partners with shaded patios and cold drinks—making them the ideal spots to watch the arrival comfortably while supporting the local businesses that make our live camera network possible.

Best Viewing Spots Around the Bay:

1. Point Loma
Cabrillo National Monument (By the Cabrillo Statue): If you want to be the very first to see her, this is the spot. Standing by the Cabrillo statue provides an incredible, elevated vantage point for the first visual as the carrier approaches from the Pacific, enters the bay, and makes her turn east into the greater channel.
Note: National Park entrance fees apply and parking can fill up. There are minimal concessions (only a few vending machines), so bring lots of your own water. No pets allowed.
Double-Viewing Tip: Once the ship passes Point Loma, you might have just enough time to head down to Seaport Village to catch her pulling into the pier. If you are driving yourself, plan your route in advance and park in the Seaport Village pay lot (be prepared to pay)—it is your only chance at getting there and parked before the carrier pulls in. Otherwise, ride Uber/Lyft. Crucial note: Stay up top by the statue! If you venture down to the tide pools, there is no cell service, so you will not be able to call a rideshare from down there.

2. Shelter Island
Fathom Bistro Bait & Tackle (On the Shelter Island Fishing Pier): Home to one of our live cameras and the first to see her enter the channel. You are right over the water as the carrier makes its initial approach into the channel. Grab cold craft beers, sodas, and snacks right on the pier.

Bali Hai Restaurant (North End): Outstanding open water views of the bay and downtown skyline. Their covered outdoor bayside dining lets you get out of the direct sun. Reservations are strongly recommended.

Shoreline Walkways: Grassy parks and walking paths line the eastern bayfront. There are benches and open sightlines all the way down Shelter Island Drive.  Any spot is a good one.

3. Harbor Island
Tom Ham's Lighthouse: Host to our east (city) and south (channel entrance) facing bay cams. The outdoor patio offers panoramic views right at the bend where the carrier turns into the main bay channel. A world-class vantage point out of the direct sun. Reservations are strongly recommended.

Harbor Island Shoreline: A continuous, scenic sidewalk runs the entire length of the island. It offers front-row views as the carrier enters the bay and swings toward the NAS North Island turning basin. Note: Standing along the path is exposed to the sun—bring hats and sunscreen.

4. Seaport Village & Tuna Harbor
Mike Hess Brewing Company - Seaport Village: Host to our camera directly across the water from the Naval Air Station North Island (NASNI) carrier berths. Great shaded outdoor patio, cold craft beer, and refreshing drinks right across from where the Lincoln will moor.

Tuna Harbor Pier & Boardwalk: Located at the northern end of Seaport Village, steps from Mike Hess Brewing. While the narrow pier can fill up quickly, the adjacent boardwalk also offers sightlines directly across the channel to the carrier piers.

Arrival Timeline & Live Stream Schedule
24/7 Live Stream: Active now.
8:00 AM – Daily Morning Colors (USS Carl Vinson): Tune in early to observe morning colors from the USS Carl Vinson (CVN 70) and the playing of the National Anthem—a proud daily tradition on our channel.
Following Colors – Live Chat & Bay Activity: Jump into the live chat to connect with fellow viewers while stream coverage ramps up and air activity, views of spectators arriving, and support vessels begin positioning.
~10:30 AM – First Visual Sighting: Expected first visual of CVN-72  south of Point Loma.

Surprise Pop-Up Cam: In addition to our fixed bay cameras, keep an eye on the broadcast for a special pop-up angle powered by our portable Starlink rig. We are working on deploying a brand-new, exciting vantage point specifically for this arrival—tune in to the live stream to see where it lands!

Pro-Tip for In-Person Spectators:
Even if you are watching live from the waterfront, keep our live feed pulled up on your phone. You’ll be able to listen in on real-time marine radio chatter.

Where to Watch Online:
A live feed will launch on our Facebook page close to arrival (be sure to follow), but our primary, uninterrupted broadcast will stream on YouTube (https://t.co/CJRBV5w1hq) - be sure to subscribe, it's free. The YouTube feed streams in full high definition with higher bitrate and pristine audio, free from automated Facebook censors.

Show Your Support!
Make sure to bring your American flags and yellow ribbons! As the Lincoln pulls into the bay, the crew will be "manning the rails" along the flight deck. The ship passes close enough to the shoreline that they can easily see and hear the crowds lining the bay. Let’s wave those flags, cheer loudly, and give them the thunderous San Diego welcome home they deserve!

Nearby Accommodations (Walking Distance)
If you are staying overnight near the waterfront to beat morning traffic:
Shelter Island: Bay Club Hotel and Marina San Diego, California,  Best Western Plus Island Palms Hotel & Marina, and Humphreys Half Moon Inn. (Hotels sit along the western marina side; simply cross Shelter Island Drive to reach the bayfront viewing path).
Harbor Island: Sheraton San Diego Resort and Hilton San Diego Airport/ Harbor Island. Both are an easy walk to the sidewalk on the bay side.

For visitors staying outside these areas, rideshares (Uber/Lyft) are strongly encouraged, as parking along both islands might be difficult if you arrive later.
Sun & Weather Notice

With temperatures expected in the mid-80s across the waterfront, please bring plenty of water, wear a hat, and apply sunscreen if you plan to stand outside.
