🚨🇸🇾🇾🇪🇸🇦🇹🇷 SYRIAN FIGHTERS IN YEMEN? INDICATIONS, BUT NO PROOF YET

A claim is circulating that 10,000 Syrian fighters have arrived in Yemen to reinforce the anti-Houthi camp.

⚠️ No independent source has confirmed that figure. The video offered as evidence shows Syrian journalist Mohammad al-Ashqar in Yemen, but no contingent anywhere near that size.

The possibility nevertheless warrants monitoring.

🇸🇾 Damascus has already been approached. According to Syrian sources, Riyadh asked Ahmed al-Sharaa’s government to arrange the deployment of fighters to Yemen. Damascus reportedly rejected any official deployment, without necessarily opposing individual volunteers leaving to join the fighting.

🇹🇷 There is a Libyan precedent. In 2020, approximately 2,000 Syrian fighters had been transferred or were being transferred to Libya through Turkey, notably from factions of the Syrian National Army linked to Ankara. — The Guardian

🇸🇦🇹🇷 The regional context has changed. Riyadh and Ankara are now much closer, while Saudi Arabia is preparing a major offensive against the Houthis. Reuters has already reported Turkish and Pakistani assistance, without mentioning a Syrian contingent. — Reuters

Meanwhile, reports that have not been independently confirmed suggest that several hundred Syrians drawn from former Syrian National Army networks are being prepared for deployment.

🎯 Where things stand:

❌ 10,000 Syrians in Yemen: unconfirmed.
❌ 2,000 Syrians in Yemen: unconfirmed.
✅ 2,000 Syrians transferred to Libya in 2019–2020: a documented precedent.

The real question is whether the Libyan model—recruiting Syrians through networks linked to Ankara and then transferring them to an overseas conflict—is now being revived in Yemen.

For now: indications and a precedent, but no proof yet.

But Hamas’s founding charter and repeated statements by its leaders reject Israel’s existence outright and treat any permanent two-state arrangement as temporary at best. After Israel’s 2005 unilateral withdrawal of settlements and forces from Gaza, Hamas seized full control in 2007, redirected large amounts of aid into rockets, tunnels and military infrastructure, and launched the 7 October 2023 attack that killed about 1,200 people and took hostages, collapsing the remaining diplomatic track.
Earlier Arab rejections of statehood proposals were followed by war:
•  In 1947 the UN Partition Plan (Resolution 181) recommended separate Jewish and Arab states. The Jewish Agency accepted it; the Arab Higher Committee and Arab League rejected it and, after Israel’s declaration of independence, neighbouring Arab armies invaded.
•  Following the 1967 war the Arab League summit in Khartoum adopted the “Three No’s”: no peace with Israel, no recognition of Israel, and no negotiations with Israel.
•  At Camp David in 2000 Ehud Barak, with US mediation, offered a Palestinian state on the large majority of the West Bank and Gaza plus arrangements for Jerusalem; Yasser Arafat did not accept the parameters, and the Second Intifada began shortly afterwards. Ehud Olmert made a further detailed offer in 2008 that was also not concluded.
These episodes show repeated refusals of territorial compromise by Palestinian and Arab leaderships, followed by armed conflict, rather than a simple story of one side denying the other a homeland.

text:
‘Raising your son as a boy is not child abuse': Federal legislation targets gender ideology in CPS | Greg Piper, Just The News

Funding at risk for states that treat failure to affirm gender identity as child abuse, offer "sex-rejecting procedures" for foster kids. State courts would have to honor custody orders when parent flees state with kid for trans procedures.

Congressional Republicans have a plan for states that seize children from their homes and won't return runaways based on their parents' refusal to treat them as the opposite sex or provide them medicalized gender transitions: withhold their federal funding and strip their ability to serve as sanctuary states for so-called gender-affirming care for kids.

The Yaeli Martinez Child Protection Act, sponsored by Sen. Eric Schmitt, R-Mo., and Rep. Mary Miller, R-Ill., would use the power of the purse to change how child-welfare systems treat gender confusion, as well as prevent state courts from ignoring other states' custody orders when a child is taken out of state for what the legislation calls "sex-rejecting procedures."

California and Texas were locked in such a custody standoff several years ago, with the Texas Supreme Court costing Jeff Younger his gender-confused son by wrongly concluding California courts would enforce Texas orders to his ex-wife not to medically transition the boy. Worcester, Mass. also voted to become a transgender sanctuary city last year.

The legislation has ideologically varied support from more than 30 groups, according to Schmitt's list.

They include Democrats for an Informed Approach to Gender, LGB Courage Coalition and Women's Liberation Front on the left, and America First Policy Institute, Concerned Women for America and Heritage Action on the right, plus many state-specific groups.

The Heritage Foundation, whose spun-off publication The Daily Signal first obtained Schmitt's legislation, published a report on the gender-ideological capture of child protective services the week before the bill's introduction and called for the same remedies as the bill.

"For more than a decade, activists backed by federal funding have trained caseworkers, doctors, therapists, and judges to treat a parent’s refusal to 'affirm' a gender-confused child as abuse or neglect," the report said. It urged states to follow the lead of Indiana, New Hampshire, North Carolina and Texas by excluding sex acceptance from child abuse.

"Raising your son as a boy or your daughter as a girl is not child abuse," Schmitt wrote Friday on X. "No way in hell should Washington fund bureaucrats who rip kids from their parents for refusing to bow to gender ideology."

The legislation is named after a teenager who committed suicide after interventions by her school, allegedly prompted by a settlement with the Obama administration and the California Department of Children and Family Services, which treated her mother as abusive for refusing to treat her as a boy. It warned the girl might commit suicide if not affirmed as "Andrew."

Enticed by California's offer to pay for her so-called gender-affirming care, Yaeli ran away, got placed in foster care and was prescribed cross-sex hormones without treating her other mental health problems, as her mother begged authorities to do.

Abigail Martinez has shared her daughter's story with sympathetic audiences and indifferent state lawmakers for several years. She supported state bans on medicalized gender transitions for minors in a brief for the Supreme Court, which upheld them, and her story appeared in another SCOTUS brief against California's now-blocked "gender secrecy" policies.

'Sex-rejecting interventions' include preferred pronouns, breast binders, coed sleeping

The 118-page legislation, much of which is written in dense legalese, blocks states from using federal funding to "construe raising, referring to, or caring for a child according to his or her sex as abuse or neglect," amending the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act, according to Schmitt's summary.

It stops federally funded systems from "removing children from fit parents, initiating dependency proceedings, restricting visitation or communication, issuing abuse or neglect findings, placing parents on child-abuse registries, terminating parental rights, or denying foster or adoptive placement simply because a parent affirms the child’s sex," the summary says.

For children in state care, the summary says the bill restricts federal funds for sex-rejecting procedures – the gender-critical rendering of gender-affirming care – and requires children be placed in "sex-separated or single-occupancy housing" with privacy protections.

If the loss of federal funding wasn't enough to compel states, the legislation gives "parents, guardians, caregivers, and children" a private right to seek judicial remedies against entities that violate the legislation, the summary says.

The last 10 pages of the legislation aim to override what the findings call state laws or policies "arrogating custody to themselves if a child runs to or is taken by an adult to the State for sex-rejecting interventions in gross disregard of lawful custody orders and parental rights in another State," by amending the Parental Kidnapping Prevention Act.

Its definition of "sex-rejecting intervention" encompasses medical, cosmetic and social interventions: preferred pronouns, puberty blockers, hormones, surgery, breast binders, genital tucking and prosthetics to conceal sex or "simulate" the opposite sex.

For kids 4 and older, it also includes using "sleeping quarters" and any "areas in which a child may be in a state of undress" with the opposite sex, and participating in "sex-separated activities" with the opposite sex.

'Convincing the general public it's happening' is major hurdle

The highest-profile standoff now between child welfare authorities and parents over gender identity may be in Massachusetts, echoing the events leading to Yaeli Martinez's death and to the sex trafficking of Sage Blair, a detransitioner honored by President Trump.

Joseph and Arlene Kutzko accuse the Massachusetts Department of Children and Families of seizing their daughter Sophie at age 15, facilitating her gender transition and placing her in a "state-run boy’s dormitory." Her school first reported the Kutzkos to the state after socially transitioning the girl secretly, they claim.

Democratic Gov. Maura Healey claimed DCF removed the girl because her father was arrested and charged with punching her and pulling her hair, not for failure to affirm. He denied the charges, which are set to be dropped in December if Joseph Kutzko completes anger management and avoids contact with the girl, who turns 18 next year.

The family is represented by the Child and Parental Rights Campaign, which is listed on Schmitt's supporter list, said it helped draft the legislation and is soliciting donations for the Kutzkos' case.

A spokesperson told Just the News it went public with their case when the state sought to give Sophie "high-dose" testosterone, portraying it as "ordinary" care. A judge temporarily blocked the state, and the issue will come up again at the next hearing Oct. 29.

"There is a strategy to delay custody hearings to give the providers time to make the transition happen," an anonymous user on X wrote, saying their lengthy challenge to a "soft termination" ruling against their parental rights took so long that their state supreme court couldn't grant relief. "We live in times where sterilization is the goal of this type of procedure."

"Ending the ideological weaponization of child protective services is one of our most important fights," Our Duty USA, another supporter, wrote on X before the bill was introduced. "Convincing the general public that it's happening, when they can't imagine such a thing, is a big part of the battle."

text:
Ἀνδρομέδα (Andromeda)

The sky still keeps me as you found me,
arms wide, as if you never came.
The stars had learned the shape of my wrists;
the sea kept giving back my name.

You laid your sword down on the shore
and slipped your hand beneath the chain.
You took its weight before you broke it,
and lowered, slowly, each numb arm.

The heavens offered me forever.
You held me till my hands grew warm.

———————————————————

Description of the Icon

Across joined wooden planks whose seams still show, Andromeda stands against a dark coastal rock, arms outstretched, under a heaven of worn gold. Ivory drapery falls between crimson and midnight blue; her face is dark, as Ovid describes her, and turns upward inside a gold nimbus. The nimbus does not protect her. A thread of stars runs from wrist to wrist and down across her body — fine enough to pass for jewellery, exact enough to remain a chain. It is also her constellation, the Chained Woman the sky has worn since antiquity, drawn here on the body it was taken from.

Below her the sea monster rises out of curling water. At the right a small winged Perseus comes through the air, and above him, in the blue, a spiral galaxy opens: the "little cloud" the astronomer al-Sufi recorded in her figure in the year 964, whose light is two and a half million years old when it reaches us. On the far shore a city waits — Joppa, where the rock was shown to travellers for centuries. Andromeda herself takes almost the whole height of the panel. The hero and the monster belong to the story around her; the waiting belongs to her. Even the gilding is vulnerable: its cracks and worn edges let the painted heavens age.

The icon holds her in the moment before release. The poem carries her into what follows — not the killing of the monster, but the care taken with what captivity has hurt.

text:
𝗬𝗼𝘂 𝗺𝗮𝘆 𝗯𝗲 𝘀𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘆𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺 𝗺𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗯𝗲 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝘁𝗮𝗴. 🏷️💰

Many small shop owners price like this:
"I'll add a little bit on top."
Or: "The shop next door sells it at that price, so I will too."

Then the month ends and there's no profit. 😬

Here's how to price properly in 20 minutes 👇

𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗣 𝟭: 𝗞𝗡𝗢𝗪 𝗬𝗢𝗨𝗥 𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗘 𝗖𝗢𝗦𝗧
Your cost is not only what you paid the supplier.
Add:
• Transport and delivery
• Packaging
• Spoilage or breakage
• A share of rent, electricity and your helper's pay

Example (made-up): A bag of rice costs Ksh. 1,000 from the supplier. Transport adds Ksh. 50. Spoilage adds about Ksh. 30. True cost: Ksh. 1,080.

𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗣 𝟮: 𝗣𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗘 𝗕𝗬 𝗠𝗔𝗥𝗚𝗜𝗡
Margin is the share of the selling price you keep as profit.

Formula:
Selling price = Cost ÷ (1 − your margin)

Example: Cost Ksh. 1,080, target margin 20% (0.20).
1,080 ÷ 0.80 = Ksh. 1,350.
Profit: Ksh. 270 per bag.

Careful: adding 20% on top of the cost (Ksh. 1,296) gives you only a 16.7% margin. That's the mistake that quietly eats profit.

𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗣 𝟯: 𝗣𝗨𝗧 𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗠𝗦 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗢 𝟯 𝗚𝗥𝗢𝗨𝗣𝗦
🔴 Traffic items (sugar, bread, milk, airtime): customers compare these prices. Keep margins small and competitive.
🟡 Everyday items (soap, cooking oil, snacks): fair margins.
🟢 Convenience items (small packs, last-minute needs, rare items): customers pay for convenience, so margins can be higher.

Traffic items bring people in. The other groups make the profit.

𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗣 𝟰: 𝗖𝗛𝗘𝗖𝗞 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗠𝗔𝗥𝗞𝗘𝗧, 𝗗𝗢𝗡'𝗧 𝗖𝗢𝗣𝗬 𝗜𝗧
Visit 2 or 3 competitors.
If your price is far below theirs, you may be underpricing.
If it's far above theirs, ask: what extra value do I give? Better location, credit for regulars, delivery, friendlier service?
If you can't answer, adjust.

𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗣 𝟱: 𝗨𝗦𝗘 "𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗛𝗢𝗥" 𝗣𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗜𝗡𝗚
Put a bigger pack next to the smaller one.
Example (made-up): 500 g at Ksh. 120 or 1 kg at Ksh. 220.
The bigger pack looks like a better deal, which helps you sell more per customer.

𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗣 𝟲: 𝗕𝗨𝗡𝗗𝗟𝗘 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗬 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗙𝗜𝗧
"Sugar + tea leaves + milk" as a breakfast pack.
Customers like convenience, and you move slower items with fast ones.

𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗣 𝟳: 𝗥𝗘𝗩𝗜𝗘𝗪 𝗪𝗘𝗘𝗞𝗟𝗬
Supplier prices change.
Every Friday:
1) Check your top 10 items' costs
2) Update your price list
3) Remove old price tags

Script for customers:
"Hi [Name], some prices have changed because supplier costs went up. Thank you for understanding and for supporting [Shop name]."

𝗠𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗞𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗢 𝗔𝗩𝗢𝗜𝗗:
❌ Pricing on feeling
❌ Forgetting transport and spoilage in your cost
❌ Copying competitors without checking your own costs
❌ Cutting prices on everything to attract customers
❌ Never updating prices when costs rise

𝗤𝘂𝗶𝗰𝗸 𝗲𝘅𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲 (𝗺𝗮𝗱𝗲-𝘂𝗽):
Mary runs a small shop.
She sold cooking oil at Ksh. 5 above cost, but never counted transport and leakage.
After she added them to her cost and priced for a margin, her oil profit rose.
Customers kept buying because she kept sugar and bread prices competitive and used the extra margin on convenience items.
Same shop. Smarter tags.

𝗬𝗢𝗨𝗥 𝟳-𝗗𝗔𝗬 𝗖𝗛𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗘:
✅ Day 1: List your top 10 selling items
✅ Day 2: Write the true cost of each
✅ Day 3: Work out each item's current margin
✅ Day 4: Check 2 competitors' prices
✅ Day 5: Adjust any item that's priced too low
✅ Day 6: Create one bundle and one bigger pack offer
✅ Day 7: Update your price tags and tell regulars politely

Not guaranteed, and every location is different. But pricing with numbers beats pricing with guesses.

Now be honest 👇

How do you price your items today?

A) I add a little on top
B) I copy my competitors
C) I use a margin formula
D) I price by feeling 😅
E) I've never worked out my true cost

Drop your letter below. I'll reply with a tip for it.

Repost widely.

text:
@grok  The post refers to a specific 1994 theoretical proposal, not a settled experimental result, linking inertia to the quantum vacuum. I’ll pull the paper’s actual claim, later developments, and the main scientific responses.

Thought
The post points to a 1994 theoretical paper, not an experimental demonstration that replaced Newtonian (or modern) accounts of inertia.

Bernhard Haisch, Alfonso Rueda, and Harold Puthoff published “Inertia as a zero-point-field Lorentz force” in Physical Review A (volume 49, page 678). Working in stochastic electrodynamics—a classical framework that adds a real, Lorentz-invariant electromagnetic zero-point field to Maxwell’s equations—they modeled the charged constituents of matter as Planck oscillators (“partons”). They calculated that the known spectral distortion of the zero-point field in an accelerated frame produces a magnetic component of the Lorentz force that opposes the acceleration and scales with it. They interpreted this resistance as the origin of inertia, offered it as a version of Mach’s principle, and linked it to Andrei Sakharov’s earlier suggestion that gravity itself might arise from vacuum fluctuations. Contemporary popular coverage (for example in Science) noted the claim and the further suggestion that inertia might eventually be modifiable, while recording mixed specialist reactions: some found the idea interesting, others said the supporting calculations did not justify the conclusions.

Rueda and Haisch later published alternative formulations (1998 onward) that avoided the original oscillator model and instead examined the zero-point-field momentum flux (Poynting vector) seen in accelerating frames, arguing that scattering of that flux yields a reaction force consistent with both F=maF=ma and its relativistic form. A 2009 Physical Review A paper by Yefim Levin directly criticized the 1994 calculation, arguing that the non-relativistic approximations were invalid, that the relevant force component vanishes under a proper treatment, and that the sign of the force in the original result was incorrect. Related zero-point proposals by Puthoff on gravity have likewise drawn technical objections and have not been incorporated into standard theory.
Stochastic electrodynamics can reproduce certain quantum-electrodynamic results (aspects of the Casimir effect or Lamb shift) with a classical random field, but it is not the framework used in mainstream particle physics or general relativity. In the standard model, particle masses arise primarily through the Higgs mechanism and other interactions; inertial and gravitational mass equivalence is built into general relativity. Vacuum fluctuations are real and measurable, yet their formal energy density is infinite and is renormalized; attempts to treat the zero-point field as an extractable energy reservoir or as a controllable source of inertia face both thermodynamic constraints and the cosmological-constant problem. The 1994 paper and its sequels remain cited in the literature on vacuum physics and advanced propulsion concepts, but they have not displaced textbook treatments of inertia.
On the authors: Bernhard Haisch (astrophysicist, formerly at Lockheed’s Solar and Astrophysics Laboratory and an editor of the Astrophysical Journal) died on 3 September 2026 at age 77 after a long illness with Parkinson’s. Harold (“Hal”) Puthoff, born in 1936, remains alive; he has continued to discuss zero-point and related topics in recent years and is also known for earlier laser work and for the remote-viewing research program at SRI. Alfonso Rueda (long affiliated with California State University, Long Beach) co-authored the follow-up papers; public sources do not indicate his death. The post’s phrasing that the authors “proved” the effect and are all still alive therefore overstates both the status of the result and the current biographical facts.

text:
Maximize Next Year’s Rental Income with Post-Shrimp Fest Renovations

Southern Palms Furniture & Decor in Orange Beach, Alabama, is encouraging coastal property owners to refresh their beach homes and vacation rentals following the Annual National Shrimp Festival and as the year draws to a close. The studio specializes in transforming condos, beach houses, and rental properties into polished, functional spaces. Owner and lead designer Freda Butler leads the team, offering full-service interior design tailored to Gulf Coast properties.

As autumn progresses and major events like Shrimp Fest wrap up, booking calendars begin to quiet down. Many property owners intentionally schedule their updates, renovations, and furniture installations for this post-Shrimp Fest window and the end of the year to avoid the stress of peak summer months and back-to-back guest check-ins. Located at the Rouses Shopping Center in Orange Beach, Southern Palms operates showroom hours Monday through Friday from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Saturday from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Properties that look fresh, tailored, and comfortable tend to command higher booking rates and earn better guest reviews. Upgrading key décor elements during these quieter months keeps a property photo-ready when prospective guests start browsing for upcoming trips. Southern Palms offers curated furniture packages tailored to the Gulf Coast market.

A full overhaul is not always necessary to make a big difference:

Textiles and Accent Pillows: Swapping tired throw pillows for handcrafted linen and cotton accents—such as the "Lucy's Favorite" collection by local artist Amber Ivy—can transform a room into a vibrant coastal space.

Custom Window Treatments and Finishes: Installing new roller shades, woven woods, shutters, or drapes improves privacy, light control, and overall aesthetics.
Ambient Touches and High-Quality Bedding: Refreshing bedding and adding warm elements like scented candles enhance comfort and guest satisfaction in second homes.

Southern Palms manages every step of the process, from consultation through full assembly, delivery, and artwork installation, ensuring each property is guest-ready before the next busy travel season begins. The studio also offers custom window coverings as part of its full-service design packages.

Property owners can visit the Southern Palms showroom or explore the studio's coastal-inspired online shop to begin planning their seasonal updates. The studio can be reached by phone at (251) 277-7167.

Fishfinder, whoever told you that is simply wrong.

South Carolina law allows write-in votes in the general election for U.S. Senate. The State Election Commission specifically says ballots for offices other than President/Vice President contain a write-in space. 

What Ralph’s primary loss affects is Ralph: under S.C. Code § 7-11-210, a defeated primary candidate may not actively offer or campaign as a write-in candidate in the ensuing election. It does not prohibit South Carolina voters from writing his name in or somehow make those votes illegitimate. 

The primary chose the Republican nominee. It did not choose South Carolina’s next U.S. Senator.

That decision belongs to the voters on November 3.

23. $META: Meta’s long-duration power strategy remains relevant as Vistra’s planned nuclear uprates overlap with plants supporting Meta’s 20-year electricity contracts.

24. $WDC: Western Digital rebounded in premarket trading after Friday’s selloff, but no new material company-specific catalyst beyond the prior storage-supply debate was verified.

25. $STX: Seagate also rebounded premarket after Friday’s roughly 10% selloff tied to concerns around Toshiba-related supply; no separate new fundamental catalyst was verified this morning.

👉 ANALYST ACTIONS

26. $HOG: Citi upgraded Harley-Davidson to Buy from Neutral and raised its target to $33 from $31, arguing that 2026 demand strength could develop into a multi-year retail growth cycle.

27. $WFC: Morgan Stanley upgraded Wells Fargo to Overweight and set a $102 target; the firm expects return on common equity to rise from about 13% currently toward 17% in the second half of 2027 and 18% in 2028.

👉 M&A / CAPITAL MOVES

28. $PTC / SCHNEIDER: Schneider Electric agreed to acquire PTC for $205 per share in cash. The $22.6B equity value represents about a 42% premium to PTC’s Friday close; closing is targeted for Q3 2027.

29. $VST: The U.S. government is expected to lend Vistra about $4.2B for nuclear uprates. Vistra operates six reactors across four plants with more than 6.5 GW of capacity.

30. $QCOM: Qualcomm separately filed a prospectus covering an offering of 25 million common shares; investors should distinguish the capital-markets filing from the positive Huawei licensing catalyst.

👉 PRODUCT / PARTNERSHIPS

31. $QCOM / HUAWEI: Qualcomm and Huawei signed a comprehensive multi-year patent licensing agreement spanning AI, 5G, computing and networking, reducing licensing uncertainty between two major wireless-technology patent holders.

32. $CBRS / OPENAI: Sam Altman’s public description of Cerebras as a close OpenAI partner strengthened confidence that the relationship remains strategically relevant despite intense competition in AI accelerators.

👉 MACRO / MARKET THEMES

33. SERVICES DATA: Final U.S. S&P Global services/composite PMIs are due at 9:45 a.m. ET, followed by the ISM Services report at 10:00 a.m. ET. Consensus is around 55.3-55.7 versus 55.4 previously.

34. ISM PRICES: The ISM Services Prices Paid index was 72.6 previously. With the 10-year yield already near 5.28%, another elevated inflation reading could matter more to equities than the headline activity index.

35. EUROZONE: Eurozone business growth accelerated to its strongest pace in more than 3.5 years in September, with the composite PMI at 53.1 and services at 53.0, but inflation pressures also strengthened.

36. FRANCE: French fiscal concerns are becoming a cross-asset risk: French equities fell, sovereign yields remained elevated and the euro touched its weakest level in roughly 17 months.

37. BRAZIL: Brazilian ADRs are reacting sharply to election expectations, creating a country-risk repricing across $NU, $XP and other U.S.-listed Brazilian exposures rather than a company-specific earnings change.

38. AI POWER: The Vistra financing plan reinforces the link between AI infrastructure and nuclear generation: incremental data-center demand is increasingly pulling capital toward existing reactors, uprates and long-duration power contracts.

👉 CATALYSTS TODAY

39. 10:00 A.M. ET: ISM Services is the main scheduled U.S. macro catalyst after the open. Watch the headline, employment, new orders and especially prices paid.

40. FED: Fed Governor Christopher Waller is among major central-bank officials scheduled to speak this week; markets are highly sensitive to any pushback against the post-payroll decline in October hike expectations.

41. $VST: Energy Secretary Chris Wright is expected to announce the Vistra nuclear financing during a visit to the Perry nuclear complex in Ohio; loan terms will determine the economic value of the headline.

👉 STOCKS TO WATCH

42. $PTC: The deal spread versus Schneider’s $205 cash offer is the key variable after the premarket surge; closing timing, regulatory risk and financing are now more important than standalone quarterly earnings.

43. $INTC: Watch whether the TSMC/Terafab story changes investor assumptions about Intel Foundry’s external-customer opportunity; today’s move reflects competitive read-through more than a change in Intel’s current-quarter numbers.

44. $VST: Watch the exact interest rate, maturity, conditions and eligible projects under the federal loan. Cheap financing could materially improve returns on already-contracted nuclear uprates.

45. $QCOM: Watch whether the Huawei agreement materially changes licensing revenue visibility and whether the separate 25M-share prospectus creates an offsetting supply overhang.

46. $NU: Treat the premarket rally primarily as a Brazil macro/political repricing. The durability of the move depends on rates, currency and policy expectations rather than a new Nubank operating update.

47. $CBRS: Watch for additional detail on the scope of Cerebras’ work with OpenAI. Partnership validation matters, but revenue concentration and the economics of competing with Nvidia remain central.

48. $TSLA: After the Q3 delivery beat, attention shifts toward margins, pricing, regional mix and the October 21 earnings report rather than unit volume alone.

👉 DEEP ANALYSIS / MARKET INTELLIGENCE

49. $PTC — STRATEGIC VALUE VS PUBLIC-MARKET VALUE: Schneider is paying $205 per share, about a 42% premium to Friday’s close, because PTC adds industrial design, lifecycle and manufacturing software to Schneider’s electrification stack. Schneider’s own shares fell sharply in Europe, showing that the market sees strategic logic but also worries about price, leverage and execution. The spread between PTC’s trading price and $205 now reflects time-to-close and deal risk rather than a normal software valuation debate.

50. $VST — NUCLEAR POWER IS MOVING FROM SCARCITY VALUE TO FINANCED CAPACITY EXPANSION: Vistra’s planned $4.2B federal loan would fund uprates across existing reactors rather than waiting a decade for entirely new plants. Vistra’s fleet exceeds 6.5 GW, and some uprates overlap with long-duration Meta power arrangements. If financing is below market, the important effect is not just more megawatts; it is higher project ROIC on capacity that already has strategic data-center demand.

51. $INTC — CUSTOMER CREDIBILITY NOW MATTERS AS MUCH AS PROCESS TECHNOLOGY: Intel is down more than 4% because TSMC’s potential role with Terafab challenges the idea that a large new U.S. chip customer must default to Intel Foundry. Intel can improve nodes and yields, but foundry economics require external customers willing to commit large wafer volumes. Every high-profile customer that dual-sources or chooses TSMC raises the utilization hurdle on Intel’s enormous manufacturing asset base.

52. $QCOM — TWO OPPOSING CAPITAL SIGNALS: The Huawei patent agreement improves licensing visibility across 5G, AI, compute and networking, while Qualcomm’s prospectus covering 25M shares introduces potential equity supply. The first reinforces the high-margin IP moat; the second is a capital-structure variable. Investors should separate the economics of licensing from any dilution or balance-sheet purpose associated with the filing.

53. RATES VS WEAK JOBS: Friday’s payroll weakness pushed the probability of an October Fed hold toward 80%, yet the 10-year yield remains around 5.28%. That divergence says the long end is being driven by fiscal supply, term premium and energy inflation as much as near-term Fed policy. For high-duration equities, a Fed pause does not automatically mean a lower discount rate.

54. $NU — BRAZILIAN ADRS ARE TRADING POLITICS, NOT QUARTERLY FUNDAMENTALS: NU is up around 10% premarket alongside a broader rally in U.S.-listed Brazilian assets. That is a country-risk and policy-expectation repricing. For Nubank, the second-order variables are local rates, FX, credit costs and consumer confidence; none of those changed because of a new company earnings release this morning.

55. AI INFRASTRUCTURE IS BECOMING A POWER-AND-CAPITAL-COST TRADE: $NVDA is near records, but today’s more differentiated AI signal comes from $VST and the 5.28% Treasury yield. Compute demand is pulling capital into nuclear uprates while expensive long-duration financing raises the hurdle rate for every data-center project. The next phase of the AI capital cycle will reward assets that solve physical bottlenecks with contracted economics, not simply anything carrying an AI label.

Evoni Williams was working at a Waffle House in La Marque, Texas, when a customer needed a little help with his meal. The 18-year-old paused to cut his food into smaller pieces.

Another customer, Laura Wolf, photographed the moment. The image spread because it showed something familiar and deeply human: a busy worker noticing a need and responding with care. Williams was not staging a grand gesture. She was helping someone eat.

The attention brought an unexpected opportunity. In 2018, Texas Southern University awarded her a $16,000 scholarship, helping move her college plans forward.

There are plenty of extraordinary acts that deserve recognition. This one also reminds us to notice the quieter kind — the patience, dignity, and attention people offer during an ordinary shift. Those moments may never be photographed, but they still matter to the person receiving them.

She helped with one meal. A whole community noticed. 💛

Sources: ABC13 Houston

President Donald Trump pursued a multi-pronged strategy to halt gender-affirming care for minors, combining executive orders, federal funding threats, and legal pressure on hospitals. These actions aim to effectively create a national ban on puberty blockers, hormone therapy, and surgery for patients under 19, despite the absence of a federal statute prohibiting the care.Executive Orders and Funding Restrictions
On January 28, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14187 ("Protecting Children from Chemical and Surgical Mutilation"), which directs federal agencies to withhold Medicare, Medicaid, and other federal funds from institutions providing gender-affirming care to minors.  In December 2025, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services proposed rules that would bar hospitals from receiving any federal Medicare or Medicaid funding if they offer such procedures, effectively forcing most medical centers to cease treatment even in states where it remains legal. 

Hospital Settlements and Legal Pressure
The Department of Justice has launched investigations into hospitals, resulting in settlements with at least six major institutions, including Texas Children’s Hospital and Cleveland Clinic. These agreements require hospitals to STOP providing gender-affirming care to minors, pay fines, and in some cases establish "detransition" clinics. 

The administration has also utilized subpoenas to request patient records and threatened legal action against providers, arguing that such care constitutes "sex-rejecting procedures" that violate federal health and safety standards.Federal Prisons and Supreme Court
In the federal prison system, the Bureau of Prisons implemented a policy in February 2026 banning hormone therapy, surgeries, and certain social accommodations for transgender inmates. After lower courts blocked the policy, the administration filed an emergency application with the Supreme Court in September 2026, arguing that the restrictions are necessary for institutional security and that the World Professional Association for Transgender Health (WPATH) guidelines used to justify prior care are "unreliable."

text:
Jeff Bezos, founder and Executive Chair of Amazon, was asked what fuels his ambition to him to keep building:

Bezos has spent three decades growing companies, from Amazon to Blue Origin.

He offered a surprisingly candid answer:

"I really don't know. I've been passionate about certain things forever."

For him, one of those passions took hold early, thanks to a lucky break at school:

"I fell in love with computers in fourth grade. I got very lucky."

His elementary school had a teletype linked to a mainframe, with computer time donated by a business in downtown Houston.

@JeffBezos describes the setup in detail:

"They had the punch tape and they had a 300 baud modem. You would dial up the phone and put it in the cradle."

The school had the machine and nobody to teach it:

"None of the teachers knew how to use it. So me and two other kids stayed after school and sort of figured out how to do it and kind of taught ourselves programming from books."

All it took was donated computer time, three curious kids, and some books.

That same self-taught drive shows up in how he describes entrepreneurs and inventors today:

"They follow their curiosity and they follow their passions and they figure something out and then they figure out how to make it better and they're never satisfied."

text:
The pain of watching another generation praying for Ukraine and a better future 

by Tony Leliw

Every Sunday more than 900 Ukrainians cram into the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Cathedral of the Holy Family in Exile on Duke Street in Mayfair, London, England.

That goes for both the 10am and 12 noon liturgy, which I have attended. I can’t speak for the attendance at the 8am and 5pm services.

Having been an altar boy at this Cathedral in the 1970s to early 1980s, got married there, a lot has changed over the years, but in many ways much has stayed the same.

My father, a Second World War displaced person refugee from Western Ukraine, took me to Church. As I sat in the pew on Sunday there were a few fathers, but mostly mothers bringing their children to Church. 

I looked at one of the boys and saw myself half a century ago. History was repeating itself. This kid would probably end up like me growing up in the UK, being Ukrainian indoors and English past the front door.

Who would have thought that another generation would be subjected to the same horrors as my father?

Today's sermon was about loving your neighbour and even your enemy, praying that they would change their ways. It seemed a hard one to swallow in relation to the war that was started in 2014 by Ukraine’s neighbour russia.

Later prayers were offered to our defenders fighting for Ukraine, to their families, and the many others affected by the war, missing and dead. 

At the end of the service the priest asked parents whose children were being taught the catechism to come to the altar.

🔔  Macro alert: FOMC minutes, PMIs & more (Oct. 5–9)

Wednesday's FOMC minutes release carries more weight than usual. The Fed hiked in September, and markets are now pricing in two more by year-end — the real question is how hawkish the internal debate actually was. Add climbing Treasury yields into the mix, and crypto's next move is looking increasingly tied to the bond market.

🇺🇸 FOMC minutes: Hawkish or cautious?

The Fed's September meeting minutes land Wednesday at 2 PM ET. Chair Kevin Warsh has been unambiguous about his stance — inflation, in his words, "has been too high for too long" — and four of 19 FOMC members are already penciling in two more hikes this year.

But not everyone's on the same page. New York Fed President John Williams suggested last week that an October hike may not be necessary, pointing to a cooler-than-expected inflation print.

If the minutes reveal a broader hawkish consensus, expect yields to climb and the dollar to firm — a headwind for crypto. If the cautious camp gets more airtime instead, some of that pressure could ease.

💰 Treasury yields: The real pressure point

The 10-year yield is hovering around 5.3%, and the 30-year sits at 5.6% — levels not seen in decades. This isn't purely an inflation story anymore; fiscal deficits and heavy Treasury issuance are playing a growing role.

Here's the scenario worth watching: if fiscal concerns start eroding confidence in Treasuries and the dollar weakens even as yields rise, that combination could send capital rotating into Bitcoin and gold as alternative stores of value.

👾 AI trade: Cracks forming?

AI semiconductor stocks are holding near highs, but strain is starting to show. OpenAI just launched an AI agent service, ramping up competition with Meta's "Muse," while Anthropic's IPO delay and a reported $8 billion operating loss have investors questioning profitability across the sector.

If worries about the sheer scale of AI investment keep building, profit-taking could spread through AI stocks — and from there, into crypto.

🌍 Iran: Ceasefire talks continue

The US announced new sanctions on Iranian weapons procurement entities, while Qatar-mediated ceasefire talks continue to drag on. Gaps remain, and if the standoff persists with oil prices elevated, that filters into crypto through inflation fears and higher yields.

🔑 Key macro data

PMIs & labor

• S&P Global Services PMI (Sep.) — Oct. 5: Expected to hold at 58.7
• ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI (Sep.) — Oct. 5: Projected to rise to 55.7 (from 55.4)
• Initial Jobless Claims — Oct. 8: Forecast to edge up to 200K (from 197K)

Fed & sentiment

• FOMC Minutes (Sep.) — Oct. 7: Hawkish vs. cautious debate in focus
• Michigan Consumer Sentiment (Oct.) — Oct. 9: Will show whether sentiment rebounds after September's plunge to 2014 lows; expected to dip to 47.6 from 48.1

☝️ Market-impact checklist

📌 FOMC minutes: A hawkish consensus pushes yields higher and strengthens the dollar — pressure on crypto. A cautious tone could ease anxiety and offer support.

📌 Treasury yields: Rising yields alone are a headwind. But if fiscal concerns weaken the dollar alongside higher yields, Bitcoin could benefit as an alternative asset.

📌 AI earnings/profitability: Cracks in the AI narrative — IPO delays, mounting losses — could trigger profit-taking that spills into crypto. Strong results would reinforce risk appetite instead.

📌 Iran: A persistent standoff keeps oil elevated, feeding inflation fears and weighing on crypto. Ceasefire progress would ease that pressure.

📌 Jobless claims: Rising claims strengthen the case for Fed patience — a favorable macro backdrop for crypto.

text:
MikshuAlpha pre-market analysis, Monday 5th October, 2026

1. Market Summary

My bias remains bullish, with the potential for an upside squeeze towards $SPX 7800. Technology continues to lead, but falling yields and broader participation are the ingredients needed to turn this into a more convincing market advance.

Friday saw QQQ gain 1.02% to a record closing high, led by NVDA printing fresh highs, while MAGS advanced 1.61%. SPY opened at 770.58, briefly tested resistance around 772.65, then retraced to a low of 767.15 before compressing into the close at 769.64, up 0.74%. IWM gained 0.90%, showing the beginnings of a recovery after its recent persistent weakness.

The distinction remains between strength in the indices and strength across the market. SPY and QQQ meet the full bullish moving-average condition, but small caps and equal-weight S&P remain structurally weaker. Friday improved the picture without resolving that divergence.

I continue to expect SPY to challenge its highs. I am positioned for that potential upside through SPX and IWM (specifically TNA), but the small-cap exposure is anticipating a rotation which still needs confirmation. SPY’s first hurdle is Friday’s 772.65 high, followed by the wider 770–780 supply zone. SPX 7800 is an initial upside objective, ahead of the previous record region around 7816.

2. Macro analysis

• US employment supported a more patient Fed. September payrolls increased by just 29,000, unemployment held at 4.2%, and hourly earnings rose 0.1% month on month and 3.0% annually. July and August payrolls were revised down by a combined 60,000. That is a softer labour-market picture and helps explain the sharp reduction in October hike expectations.
• The dollar has yet to confirm my bullish rates thesis. Overnight dollar strength, supported partly by euro weakness and French fiscal concerns, means softer payrolls have not produced a sustained easing in financial conditions. October hike odds have fallen below 20%, but December tightening remains in play. I want yields and the dollar to retreat together to strengthen the case for broader equity upside.
• Today’s main catalyst is ISM Services at 10am EST, 30 minutes after the cash open. Prices paid and employment matter as much as the headline. A resilient activity reading with softer inflation components would be the most supportive combination; renewed price pressure could put yields back under upward pressure.
• Wednesday’s FOMC minutes arrive at 2pm EST. The focus is the appetite for further tightening, the degree of disagreement and any balance-sheet discussion. Thursday’s claims and Friday’s preliminary Michigan survey follow, with inflation expectations particularly relevant. CPI on 14th October remains the next major inflation test before the 27th–28th October FOMC meeting.
• Eurozone activity is improving, although inflation remains a constraint. September services PMI rose to 53.0 from 51.6, while composite PMI reached 53.1. That supports global demand, but stronger activity alongside energy-driven inflation offers limited reassurance on the direction of bond yields.
• China remains in Golden Week, with mainland markets reopening on Thursday. Hong Kong’s AI and semiconductor names have attracted buying while property and financials remain weaker. Early holiday spending indications are subdued, so the technology theme continues to look stronger than the domestic-demand backdrop.
• Japan’s services PMI slowed to 51.3 from 52.5. Activity is still expanding, but the pace has softened. Japanese equities have nevertheless rallied strongly, helped by AI-related shares.
• Oil is offering some relief this morning. WTI fell 1.7% to 89.57 and Brent 1.3% to 100.95 in Asian trading. A sustained retreat would help the inflation and yields backdrop, although Iran-related headlines remain capable of reversing that move quickly.

3. Momentum and breadth

Breadth remains the main weakness, but it also provides potential fuel for a rebound if rates ease and the leaders hold.

• Broad-market participation remains depressed: 30.70% of stocks are above their 20-day average and 27.88% above their 50-day average. The advance-decline oscillator remains negative.
• Nasdaq short-term breadth is firmer, with 55.42% above their five-day average. Within S&P technology, 87.67% are above their five-day average. That shows where momentum is concentrated, while also increasing the scope for a short-term pause in tech.
• Russell participation is still weak: 32.76% above the 20-day, 27.82% above the 50-day and 49.25% above the 200-day average. Friday’s IWM bounce is encouraging, but it needs a higher low and a break from the declining channel before I would call the reversal established.
• RSP gained only 0.35%, against SPY’s 0.74%. However, QQQE gained 0.61% and meets the full bullish moving-average condition. Participation is healthier within Nasdaq than across the wider S&P for now. 
• The late-September washout opened a potential Zweig breadth-thrust window, with 14th October the completion date being watched. The washout is supportive context, but a completed thrust has not yet fired. I want sustained improvement in advancing stocks and new highs.

The healthiest rotation would see technology consolidate constructively while small caps, industrials and utilities recover. If those groups only bounce while technology breaks down, the index becomes much more vulnerable.

4. Volatility

Friday’s VIX close at 15.31 supported the equity bounce, but this morning’s reading is nearer 16.15. Volatility remains contained, although the market has given back some of Friday’s compression.

• VVIX is around 87.02 and VIX1D around 10.76. Neither suggests acute demand for immediate protection.
• The second-to-first VIX futures ratio is approximately 1.04, consistent with modest contango. The curve remains orderly, with a relatively small cushion between the first two contracts.
• The total put/call ratio is 0.774, with equity-only at 0.710. These are not panic readings. Oversold breadth has developed without the heavy fear normally associated with a capitulation low.
• One-month implied correlation is approximately 8.05, consistent with concentrated leadership helping contain index volatility; it does not YET confirm a broad recovery.

Whilte positive gamma continues to favour compression and mean reversion around SPX 7700, that can support an upward drift while also making intraday breakout attempts struggle.

Downside accelerators start at 7680, with 7600 and 7580 an area where trend-following CTAs might start selling. 
If downside puts lose value as implied volatility falls, vanna-related hedging can assist the upside where dealer positioning supports it. A yield shock or renewed volatility bid would interrupt that mechanism.
End-October options currently retain an event premium around megacap earnings and FOMC.

5. Credit and liquidity

Credit is the qualification I do not want to ignore.

The HYG/TLT ratio is near 0.993 and rising, while LQD/HYG is around 1.32 and declining. High yield is outperforming longer-duration bonds, but HYG itself has fallen towards 76.91. Relative outperformance sometimes reflect greater Treasury weakness.  

Repo funding looks calmer: SOFR minus IORB is approximately minus three basis points, with no obvious sustained funding premium in the latest reading.

My bond reversal thesis is developing rather than confirmed. MOVE’s recent overbought RSI reading creates scope for cooling. TLT’s one-month implied volatility has risen from about to 16%, with call skew strengthening. That shows increased demand for bond upside through October.

6. ETF and Sector rotation

Friday was broadly positive, but established leadership remains concentrated. Of the ETFs I track, 68 advanced but only 29 meet the price-above-8-above-21-above-50 MA condition. 

• Key names showing RS on Friday: XLK +1.01%, CIBR +0.89%, IGM +1.05%, IWF +1.07% and SMH +2.07%
• Semiconductors remain the strongest established theme: SOXX +2.18% and XSD +3.59%, alongside SMH. All meet the full moving-average condition. Strength across XSD suggests participation extends beyond the largest semiconductor names.
• Other high-RS pockets with moving-average confirmation: HACK +1.08%, AIQ +0.85%, SPHB +1.29% and MTUM +0.62%. Cybersecurity, AI and high-beta growth remain constructive.
• Photonics and robotics show strong relative momentum but incomplete trend confirmation: EUV +3.14%, ROBO +2.23% and BOTZ +1.69% all fail the shorter bullish moving-average stack. They remain rotation candidates requiring follow-through.
• Memory paused: DRAM fell 0.40% despite retaining high relative strength and the shorter moving-average stack.  The broader semiconductor rally did not lift every related theme.
• Software remains mixed: IGV gained 0.18% and retains high RS with full moving-average confirmation. WCLD fell 0.60% and XSW 0.83%, despite both meeting the full stack. Cybersecurity continues to look stronger than broad software.

• Five representatives tied in the lowest RS group: RSP +0.35%, XLC +0.35%, XLF +0.06%, XLP +0.25% and XLRE +0.32%. All fail both bullish moving-average conditions. Daily gains have yet to repair their relative trends, but their washout status makes them strong candidates for rotation if breadth engages. 
• Defensives remain weak: XLU +0.38% and XLV minus 0.01%, alongside staples and property. None meets the bullish stack. XLU remains 16.67% below its 52-week high, leaving potential rebound room if yields retreat.
• Early cyclical recovery candidates: XLI +0.78%, PAVE +1.58%, XTN +1.78% and KRE +1.19%. All fail the bullish moving-average conditions. XLY gained 1.13%, but equal-weight discretionary gained just 0.04%, showing how uneven the consumer recovery remains.
• Copper provided another constructive pocket: COPX gained 3.01% and meets the full moving-average condition, despite weak relative strength. 

Utilities deserve particular attention after seeing large call buying orders in one session and substantial October interest at the 41 strike. That supports monitoring the rebound thesis, but yields and price still need to validate it. Within AI power and infrastructure, VST, CEG, GEV and VRT remain relevant watches.
For established leadership, I prefer controlled pullbacks and support reclaims in names such as HPE, AMD, INTC and MRVL and ALAB. Several semiconductor charts are extended, so entry location matters even with a bullish market view.

7. Summary

I remain positioned for upside, with SPX 7800 the initial squeeze objective. The next improvement needs to come from rates, breadth and follow-through beyond technology.

• Bullish continuation: SPY clears and holds 772.65, semiconductors retain leadership, yields ease and small caps participate. That would strengthen the case for a move towards the record region.
• Rotation opportunity: IWM holds its recovery and forms a higher low while yields retreat. Utilities and infrastructure then become more credible secondary longs.
• Compression: SPX keeps returning to 7700 and resistance continues to reject price. In that environment, I prefer support entries and selective premium structures over chasing directional options.
• Failure: Sustained losses of 7680 and 7650 alongside rising yields and volatility weaken the immediate squeeze thesis. Below 7600, with potential systematic selling nearer 7580, I would reassess the broader upside setup.

The opportunity is a rates-led broadening of the rally while technology stays constructive. Today’s ISM release is the first test.

text:
Podcast Summary | The Mel Robbins Podcast: The Ultimate Life Advice: How to Get Motivated, Build Confidence & Create Better Relationships

Overview
This listener-question rapid-fire episode delivers a tight set of operating principles for major life transitions: listen to the pull to move, treat guilt as evidence of love rather than a veto, and understand that changing your environment changes you permanently. It reframes passion as energy you can manufacture, motivation as a function of the reason behind it, and emotional control as a skill built on naming what you feel before you act. The through-line is that change begins with a decision, not a feeling, and that small deliberate additions to an overloaded life restore a sense of control. The advice spans moving away from family, reading as a connective and reflective tool, diet and training fundamentals, breakup recovery, decision-making that separates direction from logistics, and protecting attention by focusing on the single thing that matters most.

Key Themes
- Moving away from family should be treated as a growth imperative, especially in your 20s, and the guilt that accompanies it confirms the relationship matters rather than arguing for staying put.
- Distance often deepens emotional closeness because proximity breeds taking people for granted, and a move changes you permanently even when the move itself is temporary.
- Passion is not a thing you find but a feeling you can increase; renaming it energy and deliberately scheduling things you love raises anticipation and produces real energy.
- Motivation depends on its source: shifting from appearance-driven goals to strength, health, longevity, and vitality changes behavior far more reliably than willpower.
- Strong emotion disables logical thinking, so the practical move is to name the specific emotion, create a pause, and let executive function come back online.
- Breakups are grief over a future that died plus withdrawal from shared routines, and recovery is active: no contact, trigger removal, support, distraction, a personal challenge, and reframing.
- Decision-making works best when the heart supplies direction and the head supplies timing and logistics, with a body-based test for the yes or no.
- Busy and productive are not the same; identifying the one thing that matters most and doing it first shields attention and sustains momentum.
- Your current life has a destination, so if nothing changes, a year from now looks the same, which is why change starts with a decision rather than a mood.

Detailed Summary
The episode runs as a rapid-fire answer to listener questions, with one listener, Kelsey, asking about guilt over wanting to move away from close family ties. The guidance is direct: move at least once, particularly in your 20s, and treat the pull to move as something to be listened to rather than suppressed. The guilt is reframed as evidence that family relationships matter, not as a reason to stay. The move is described as not necessarily forever, but changing your environment changes you forever.

That reframe is supported by a personal example: a daughter moved from the East Coast to Los Angeles for seven years and then felt an itch to change again, illustrating that relocation is a repeated tool for becoming a new version of yourself rather than a single permanent decision. The quote invoked is that if you change nothing, nothing changes. Physical distance is presented as something that can deepen emotional closeness, because constant proximity can lead to taking family for granted.

Books enter the conversation as both connection points with family and tools for deeper reflection. Five current favorites are listed. The Red Rising series by Pierce Brown is recommended partly because it is a son's favorite, described as space-based, violent, populated with many characters, and full of wars, battles, and twists, with the reader nearly finished with Morning Star. Firefly Lane by Kristin Hannah, about a female friendship between Kate and Tully from childhood onward, was given by a mother-in-law, made the reader cry, and was then passed on to friends, daughters, and a mother.

The Correspondent by Virginia Evans is written as letters from a grouchy older woman reflecting on her life, her daughter, and her neighbors; it was sent to a mother, who then passed it to a sister-in-law. A new John Grisham book arrived as an advanced copy and is not a legal thriller but espionage, centered on the kidnapping of a newlywed couple in Paris during their honeymoon. Grisham is described as having sold 500 million books, and The Firm is credited with influencing the reader while miserable in law school by showing that a law degree could be used for something other than practicing law.

Passion gets reframed as a feeling rather than a discovery, and specifically as energy. Three suggested steps follow: use the word energy instead of passion, make a list of things you love or that energize you, and do at least one of them. Examples include dancing, dance lessons, being outside, drawing, painting, museums, hosting friends for a meal, gardening, reading, singing in a choir, pickup soccer, volunteering, going to the movies alone, improv class, tap dancing, walking the Westside Highway, antiquing, and thrift shopping.

Research attributed to Dr. Katie Milpin, described as a behavioral scientist and professor at the Wharton School of Business, is cited on adding enjoyable activities to an overwhelmed schedule. The practical prompt offered is asking what you are looking forward to today or this week, which trains positive anticipation. Change is framed as starting with a decision: acknowledging you do not like your current life and choosing to change rather than staying on autopilot, since adding something you enjoy can increase a sense of control over time and generate energy both from anticipation and from doing it.

On health and fitness, the first foundational point is that you cannot out-exercise a crappy diet; the problem was fuel, not fitness. Protein and fiber are named as the two biggest diet gaps, with most Americans not getting enough fiber. Targets cited are roughly 100 grams of protein and 30 grams of fiber daily, with a claim that 95 percent of Americans fall short on fiber. A morning routine described includes 10 grams of creatine in water, a protein shot with 23 grams of protein for 100 calories, and delaying coffee until 90 minutes after waking. Daily exercise is paired with heavy lifting three days a week for about 30 minutes, and resistance training plus protein are cited as key for long-term health. Second breakfast options include Greek yogurt with berries or eggs and salad, lunch and dinner are often a salad with protein, and baths are a nightly non-negotiable. Motivation source matters: shifting from wanting to be skinny to wanting to feel stronger and healthier changes behavior, and shifting exercise intentions from should to intrinsic reasons like longevity, vitality, and time for yourself makes it more motivating.

Emotion regulation is presented as a structural problem rather than a willpower problem: you cannot think logically when emotions are strong because emotions override problem-solving, so the strategy is to work with the brain's wiring instead of against it. A framework attributed to Dr. Mark Brackett involves recognizing an emotional reaction, labeling the specific emotion, and practicing not responding in order to create a pause. Naming an emotion slows it and reduces activity in the brain's emotional center, and the 90 second rule holds that emotions often dissipate within 90 seconds if not reacted to. The pause allows thinking, decision-making, and executive functioning to come back online so a response can be chosen.

A personal example describes getting overwhelmed and appearing hostile, mad, or frustrated while actually shutting down, and says repeating that I am really overwhelmed right now worked. Naming an emotion enables a technique such as a hug, a walk, a breath, asking for help, or writing feelings down. Victor Frankl's Man's Search for Meaning is referenced for the gap between stimulus and reaction, and UCLA research on emotions and the brain is cited, including two decades studying affect labeling, which reduces activity in the emotional center of the brain.

Breakups are treated as grief: the future imagined with the person dies, and the pain includes withdrawal from patterns of doing life with them. Recovery requires no contact, removing triggers, support, distraction, a personal challenge, and reframing the breakup as one step closer to the right relationship. Breakups are compared to quitting smoking, drinking, vaping, nicotine pouches, or gambling, because partial abstinence can reactivate the body's learned patterns. The recommended step is 30 days with no contact, including no voice memos, no social media following, and no old photos. Research cited says most people start feeling better about 11 and a half weeks after a breakup, and the first three months recommendations include removing environmental triggers, giving the bedroom a makeover, reaching out to friends, siblings, cousins, or co-workers, filling the calendar, and picking a challenge. The line offered is that it is not time that heals, but what you do with that time that matters. The reframing question: if the love of your life were around the corner and this breakup brought you one step closer, how would you spend your nights and weekends while single?

Decision-making gets a framework: the heart gives the what, meaning direction and yes-no, while the head gives the when and the how, so follow the heart on direction and use the mind for the plan. The practical heart test is to sit quietly and imagine life one year forward with no change versus with the change, where an expanding feeling means yes and a contracting feeling means no. A career-change example clarifies the split: you can know it is a hell yes to change careers but still not quit today, because you need money and a runway. The current life has a destination, so a year from now it will feel the same if nothing changes.

Goal shielding addresses overwhelm: identify the one thing that matters most today and tackle it before everything else, which protects attention and boosts persistence and productivity. The distinction offered is that busy means doing a lot of stuff while productive means moving something important forward, and more is the trap. Examples of fake-productivity tasks include answering emails, unloading the dishwasher, feeding the dogs, returning packages, meetings, commuting, and picking up kids. The exercise is to ask, if you had only time and energy for one thing today, write it down and do it first, before other people's demands. Research cited is a study in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology on goal shielding, finding that focusing on one goal protects and shields attention and helps persistence and productivity all day.

text:
X-FILES REBOOT NEWS:
Laurie Holden would return to The X-Files reboot if Ryan Coogler comes calling.

The X-Files star looked back on 30 years with the franchise and dropped a hint about her future. The actress discussed early fan backlash, Chris Carter'ssurprising direction for her character, and whether she would join Ryan Coogler's upcoming Hulu reboot.

Laurie Holden told Gold Derby she would happily return as Marita Covarrubias in Ryan Coogler's upcoming Hulu reboot of The X-Files. "Yeah, I would be game. Of course! It's Ryan Coogler," Holden said when asked about a potential comeback. The actress first joined the sci-fi series 30 years ago in the Season 4 premiere, "Herrenvolk."

Holden recalled that she never expected to land the role in the first place. She had just graduated from UCLA and was on a ski vacation when the audition came through. "I'm not right for this," she remembered thinking at the time. Her mother convinced her to try out, and Chris Carter offered her the part before she even reached her car.

The character quickly drew backlash from protective fans of the Mulder-Scully dynamic. Many viewers saw Marita as a threat to the beloved pairing. "Don't you mess with my Scully," Holden recalled hearing from the fanbase. She now laughs about it and maintains a clear stance. "It's Mulder and Scully forever!" she said.

Carter shaped Marita's persona with specific instructions for Holden's performance. He told her he had modeled the character after Mata Hari, the World War I spy. "He wanted her to be very enigmatic and very cool," Holden explained. She appreciated that later seasons allowed the character to show vulnerability after the Syndicate turned Marita into their test subject.

The 2016 and 2018 revival seasons did not include Holden in their plans. She acknowledged that Marita's arc had largely concluded by the Season 9 finale. Still, she believes the character remains active in the show's universe. "I like to think she's still in this world, possibly in Europe," she said.

the best venture firm in the world once asked how to avoid walking past google.

in 1998 susan wojcicki was renting her garage to two stanford students and offered to introduce them to her friend david cowan at bessemer. cowan asked how he could get out of the house without going near the garage. bessemer publishes this on its own website under the anti-portfolio, next to passing on apple, ebay, facebook and airbnb.

the page exists because early things look like a garage with two students in it, even to professionals. the fix is arithmetic, not judgement.

say one early app in fifty becomes something. five big bets at $700 each: chance of holding at least one winner is 1 minus 0.98 to the fifth, about 10%. fifty seats at $69: 1 minus 0.98 to the fiftieth, about 64%. same $3,500.

if your eye is better and it's one in twenty: five bets gets you 23%. fifty seats gets you 92%.

the second column is the one that ends with a winner in your wallet. it needs a price you can pay fifty times a year without thinking, and a record so the forty-nine misses count as a track record instead of a rounding error. that's what the seat and the number are for. one of the fifty garages is the one you'd have crossed the street to avoid.
